sentences.zh: __FORCETOC__魏徵魏徵，字玄成，魏州曲城人。

translations.literal: __FORCETOC__Wei Zheng, Wei Zheng, style name Xuancheng, was a man of Qucheng in Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: __FORCETOC__Wei Zheng, whose style name was Xuancheng, was a native of Qucheng in Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 少孤，落魄，棄貲產不營，有大志，通貫書術。

translations.literal: In youth he lost his father; destitute and adrift, he abandoned his property without managing it. He had great ambition and was thoroughly versed in books and the arts.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in youth, he lived in destitution and made no effort to manage his inheritance, nurturing grand ambitions while mastering the literary and scholarly arts.

sentences.zh: 隋亂，詭為道士。

translations.literal: When the Sui fell into chaos, he falsely claimed to be a Daoist priest.
translations.idiomatic: When the Sui dynasty collapsed into turmoil, he disguised himself as a Daoist priest.

sentences.zh: 武陽郡丞元寶藏舉兵應李密，以徵典書檄。

translations.literal: Yuan Baozang, assistant magistrate of Wuyang Commandery, raised troops in response to Li Mi and appointed Wei Zheng to manage documents and proclamations.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Baozang, assistant magistrate of Wuyang Commandery, took up arms in support of Li Mi, he put Wei Zheng in charge of drafting documents and proclamations.

sentences.zh: 密得寶藏書，輒稱善，既聞徵所為，促召之。

translations.literal: When Li Mi received Yuan Baozang's letters, he always praised them; once he heard what Wei Zheng had written, he urgently summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi always praised the letters Yuan Baozang sent in—but when he learned that Wei Zheng had written them, he hurried to summon him.

sentences.zh: 徵進十策說密，不能用。

translations.literal: Wei Zheng submitted ten stratagems to persuade Li Mi, but they could not be adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng offered Li Mi ten strategic proposals, but Li Mi did not act on them.

sentences.zh: 王世充攻洛口，徵見長史鄭頲曰：「魏公雖驟勝，而驍將銳士死傷略盡；

translations.literal: When Wang Shichong attacked Luokou, Wei Zheng saw Chief Secretary Zheng Ting and said: "Though the Duke of Wei has won sudden victories, his fierce generals and crack soldiers have been killed and wounded until nearly all are gone;
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shichong attacked Luokou, Wei Zheng went to see Chief Secretary Zheng Ting and said, "Though the Duke of Wei has won rapid victories, his best generals and toughest fighters have been killed or wounded almost to the last man;

sentences.zh: 又府無見財，戰勝不賞。

translations.literal: Moreover the headquarters has no cash on hand, and victories in battle go unrewarded.
translations.idiomatic: And furthermore the headquarters has no ready funds—so even when they win, there are no rewards.

sentences.zh: 此二者不可以戰。

translations.literal: These two things mean one cannot fight.
translations.idiomatic: With these two conditions, they cannot afford to go on fighting.

sentences.zh: 若浚池峭壘，曠日持久，賊糧盡且去，我追擊之，取勝之道也。

translations.literal: If we deepen the moat and steepen the ramparts, prolonging the standoff day after day until the enemy's supplies are exhausted and they depart, then we pursue and strike them—that is the way to victory.
translations.idiomatic: If we deepen the moats and heighten the walls, draw the fight out over time, and wait until the enemy runs out of supplies and withdraws, we can pursue and defeat them—that is the path to victory."

sentences.zh: 」頲曰：「老儒常語耳！

translations.literal: " Zheng Ting said: "The stale talk of an old Confucian scholar!"
translations.idiomatic: " Zheng Ting replied, "That's the usual talk of some old bookish pedant!"

sentences.zh: 」徵不謝去。

translations.literal: " Wei Zheng made no apology and left.
translations.idiomatic: " Wei Zheng offered no thanks and walked away.

sentences.zh: 後從密來京師，久之未知名。

translations.literal: Later he followed Li Mi to the capital; for a long time he remained unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed Li Mi to the capital, but for a long time remained obscure.

sentences.zh: 自請安輯山東，乃擢秘書丞，馳驛至黎陽。

translations.literal: He volunteered to pacify and settle the eastern provinces, and was promoted to Secretary of the Palace Library, racing by post-horse to Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: He volunteered to pacify the Shandong region and was appointed Secretary of the Palace Library, then rode post-haste to Liyang.

sentences.zh: 時李勣尚為密守，徵與書曰：「始魏公起叛徒，振臂大呼，眾數十萬，威之所被半天下，然而一敗不振，卒歸唐者，固知天命有所歸也。

translations.literal: At the time Li Shiji was still holding the territory for Li Mi. Wei Zheng wrote to him, saying: "At first the Duke of Wei rose as a rebel leader, raising his arm and crying out—the throngs numbered in the hundreds of thousands, and the reach of his authority covered half the realm. Yet once he was defeated he could not recover, and in the end submitted to Tang—this shows clearly that the Mandate of Heaven had found its rightful home.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Li Shiji was still defending the territory on Li Mi's behalf. Wei Zheng wrote to him: "When the Duke of Wei first rose against the dynasty, he rallied hundreds of thousands to his banner and his influence reached across half the empire. Yet a single defeat left him unable to rally again, and in the end he submitted to Tang—clear proof that Heaven's mandate already rested elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 今君處必爭之地，不早自圖，則大事去矣！

translations.literal: Now you stand in a place where all sides must contend; if you do not plan early for yourself, the great cause will be lost!"
translations.idiomatic: You now hold a territory every power will fight over. If you do not act quickly on your own behalf, the opportunity will slip away forever!"

sentences.zh: 」勣得書，遂定計歸，而大發粟饋淮安王之軍。

translations.literal: " When Li Shiji received the letter, he settled on a plan to submit, and sent large quantities of grain to supply the army of the Prince of Huai'an.
translations.idiomatic: " After reading the letter, Li Shiji resolved to surrender and dispatched a large store of grain to supply the Prince of Huai'an's army.

sentences.zh: 會竇建德陷黎陽，獲徵，偽拜起居舍人。

translations.literal: Just then Dou Jiande captured Liyang and took Wei Zheng prisoner, falsely appointing him Attendant of the Imperial Diary.
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Jiande seized Liyang, he captured Wei Zheng and gave him the nominal title of Attendant of the Imperial Diary.

sentences.zh: 建德敗，與裴矩走入關，隱太子引為洗馬。

translations.literal: When Jiande was defeated, he fled through the passes with Pei Ju; the Hidden Crown Prince brought him in as Junior Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: After Dou Jiande's defeat, Wei Zheng fled through the passes into the heartland with Pei Ju, where the Hidden Crown Prince appointed him Junior Mentor.

sentences.zh: 徵見秦王功高，陰勸太子早為計。

translations.literal: Wei Zheng saw that the Prince of Qin's achievements were great and secretly urged the Crown Prince to take early measures.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the Prince of Qin's mounting power, Wei Zheng privately urged the Crown Prince to act before it was too late.

sentences.zh: 太子敗，王責謂曰：「爾鬩吾兄弟，奈何？

translations.literal: When the Crown Prince was defeated, the Prince of Qin rebuked him, saying: "You set us brothers at odds—what of it?"
translations.idiomatic: After the Crown Prince's defeat, the Prince of Qin confronted Wei Zheng: "You turned my brothers against me—how do you answer for that?"

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「太子蚤從徵言，不死今日之禍。

translations.literal: " He replied: "Had the Crown Prince heeded my words early, he would not have died in today's calamity."
translations.idiomatic: " Wei Zheng replied, "If the Crown Prince had taken my advice sooner, he would not have met this day's doom."

sentences.zh: 」王器其直，無恨意。

translations.literal: " The Prince valued his forthrightness and bore no resentment.
translations.idiomatic: " The Prince admired his blunt honesty and held no grudge.

sentences.zh: 即位，拜諫議大夫，封钜鹿縣男。

translations.literal: At his accession to the throne, [the Emperor] appointed [Wei Zheng] Remonstrating and Advising Grand Master and enfeoffed him as Baron of Julu County.
translations.idiomatic: When the new emperor took the throne, he appointed Wei Zheng Remonstrating and Advising Grand Master and enfeoffed him as Baron of Julu County.

sentences.zh: 當是時，河北州縣素事隱、巢者不自安，往往曹伏思亂。

translations.literal: At that time, prefectures and counties in Hebei that had long served the Hidden Crown Prince and the Prince of Qi could not feel secure, and many lurked in hiding and plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, officials throughout Hebei who had long served the Hidden Crown Prince and the Prince of Qi were uneasy, and many secretly plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 徵白太宗曰：「不示至公，禍不可解。

translations.literal: Wei Zheng reported to Emperor Taizong: "Unless supreme fairness is shown, the calamity cannot be resolved."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng told Emperor Taizong, "Unless you demonstrate absolute fairness, this trouble cannot be put to rest."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「爾行安喻河北。

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "You go and peacefully instruct Hebei."
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor said, "Go and reassure the people of Hebei on my behalf."

sentences.zh: 」道遇太子千牛李志安、齊王護軍李思行傳送京師，徵與其副謀曰：「屬有詔，宮府舊人普原之。

translations.literal: " On the road he encountered the Crown Prince's Palace Attendant Li Zhian and the Prince of Qi's Protector-General Li Sixing being escorted to the capital; Wei Zheng consulted his deputy, saying: "There was recently an edict pardoning all former retainers of the palace offices.
translations.idiomatic: " On the way he encountered Li Zhian, the Crown Prince's Palace Attendant, and Li Sixing, the Prince of Qi's Protector-General, being escorted to the capital. Wei Zheng conspired with his deputy: "An edict has just been issued granting general amnesty to all former palace retainers.

sentences.zh: 今復執送志安等，誰不自疑者？

translations.literal: Now if we again seize and send Li Zhian and the others, who would not suspect for himself?"
translations.idiomatic: If we now send Li Zhian and the others under guard to the capital, who among those we are trying to reassure will not begin to doubt us?"

sentences.zh: 吾屬雖往，人不信。

translations.literal: Even if we go, people will not believe."
translations.idiomatic: Even if we make the journey ourselves, no one will trust our message."

sentences.zh: 」即貸而後聞。

translations.literal: " Immediately he released them and reported afterward.
translations.idiomatic: " He released them at once and reported his action only afterward.

sentences.zh: 使還，帝悅，日益親，或引至臥內，訪天下事。

translations.literal: When the envoy returned, the Emperor was pleased and grew daily more intimate with him, sometimes summoning him into the private quarters to inquire about affairs throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned from his mission, the emperor was delighted. Their bond deepened day by day; sometimes the emperor would summon him into his bedchamber to consult on affairs across the empire.

sentences.zh: 徵亦自以不世遇，乃展盡底蘊無所隱，凡二百餘奏，無不剴切當帝心者。

translations.literal: Wei Zheng also regarded himself as having met with an unprecedented opportunity, and so laid bare all he knew without concealment—in over two hundred memorials, not one failed to be incisive and accord with the Emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Convinced he had met with an unparalleled opportunity, Wei Zheng held nothing back. In more than two hundred memorials, each one was pointed and struck exactly where the emperor's concerns lay.

sentences.zh: 由是拜尚書右丞，兼諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Because of this he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel, concurrently serving as Remonstrating and Advising Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: On this account he was promoted to Right Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel while retaining his post as Remonstrating and Advising Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 左右有毀徵阿党親戚者，帝使溫彥博按訊，非是。

translations.literal: Those around the throne slandered Wei Zheng for showing favoritism toward his kinsmen and associates; the Emperor had Wen Yanbo investigate, and it was not so.
translations.idiomatic: Courtiers accused Wei Zheng of favoring his relatives and allies, but when the emperor had Wen Yanbo investigate, the charges proved false.

sentences.zh: 彥博曰：「徵為人臣，不能著形跡，遠嫌疑，而被飛謗，是宜責也。

translations.literal: Yanbo said: "As a subject, Wei Zheng could not make his conduct visible and keep clear of suspicion, and so suffered slander—this is something for which he should be reproached."
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo said, "As a minister, Wei Zheng failed to make his conduct transparent and keep himself above suspicion, and so became the target of malicious gossip—for that he deserves a rebuke."

sentences.zh: 」帝謂彥博行讓徵。

translations.literal: " The Emperor had Yanbo go and reproach Wei Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor sent Yanbo to admonish Wei Zheng.

sentences.zh: 徵見帝，謝曰：「臣聞君臣同心，是謂一體，豈有置至公，事形跡？

translations.literal: Wei Zheng saw the Emperor and apologized, saying: "I have heard that when ruler and minister share one heart, they are called a single body—how can one pursue supreme fairness while fussing over outward appearances?"
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Zheng saw the emperor, he replied, "I have heard that when ruler and minister are of one mind, they form a single body. How can one pursue absolute fairness while obsessing over appearances?"

sentences.zh: 若上下共由茲路，邦之興喪未可知也。

translations.literal: If above and below together follow this path, whether the state will rise or fall cannot be known."
translations.idiomatic: If both ruler and ministers go down that road together, there is no telling whether the realm will prosper or perish."

sentences.zh: 」帝矍然，曰：「吾悟之矣！

translations.literal: " The Emperor started in alarm and said: "I understand now!"
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor started, then said, "Now I see it!"

sentences.zh: 」徵頓首曰：「願陛下俾臣為良臣，毋俾臣為忠臣。

translations.literal: " Wei Zheng bowed his head and said: "I wish Your Majesty would make me a good minister, and not make me a loyal minister."
translations.idiomatic: " Wei Zheng kowtowed and said, "I ask that Your Majesty make me a good minister—not a loyal minister."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「忠、良異乎？

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "Are loyal and good ministers different?"
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor asked, "Are loyal ministers and good ministers not the same thing?"

sentences.zh: 」曰：「良臣，稷、契、咎陶也；

translations.literal: " He said: "Good ministers are men like Hou Ji, Qi, and Gao Yao;
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "Good ministers are men like Hou Ji, Qi, and Gao Yao;

sentences.zh: 忠臣，龍逢、比干也。

translations.literal: loyal ministers are men like Long Feng and Bi Gan.
translations.idiomatic: loyal ministers are men like Long Feng and Bi Gan.

sentences.zh: 良臣，身荷美名，君都顯號，子孫傅承，流祚無疆；

translations.literal: Good ministers themselves bear a fine reputation, their lords enjoy illustrious titles, their descendants inherit and transmit them, and blessings flow without end;
translations.idiomatic: Good ministers win lasting fame for themselves, bring glory to their sovereign, and leave blessings that their descendants inherit for generations;

sentences.zh: 忠臣，己嬰禍誅，君陷昏惡，喪國夷家，只取空名。

translations.literal: loyal ministers themselves meet with calamity and execution, their lords sink into folly and wickedness, the state is lost and the clan destroyed, and they gain only an empty name.
translations.idiomatic: loyal ministers suffer death and ruin themselves, leave their sovereign mired in folly and wickedness, bring down the state and destroy their clans, and gain nothing but an empty reputation.

sentences.zh: 此其異也。

translations.literal: This is the difference between them."
translations.idiomatic: That is the difference between them."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「善。

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "Well said."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Well put."

sentences.zh: 」因問：「為君者何道而明，何失而暗？

translations.literal: " Then he asked: "By what path does a ruler become enlightened, and by what fault does he become benighted?"
translations.idiomatic: " Then he asked, "What makes a ruler enlightened, and what makes him blind?"

sentences.zh: 」徵曰：「君所以明，兼聽也；

translations.literal: " Wei Zheng said: "A ruler is enlightened because he listens broadly;
translations.idiomatic: " Wei Zheng said, "A ruler is enlightened because he listens to many voices;

sentences.zh: 所以暗，偏信也。

translations.literal: he is benighted because he trusts only one side.
translations.idiomatic: he is blind because he trusts only one side.

sentences.zh: 堯、舜氏辟四門，明四目，達四聰。

translations.literal: Yao and Shun opened the four gates, clarified the four eyes, and extended the four ears.
translations.idiomatic: Yao and Shun opened the four gates of their palace, sharpened the vision of their four eyes, and extended the hearing of their four ears.

sentences.zh: 雖有共，鮌，不能塞也，靖言庸違，不能惑也。

translations.literal: Even if there were Gong Gong and Gun, they could not block [the channels of communication]; even flattering words and perverse conduct could not deceive [them].
translations.idiomatic: Even men as corrupt as Gong Gong and Gun could not choke off the flow of information, and even smooth words and perverse conduct could not mislead them.

sentences.zh: 秦二世隱藏其身，以信趙高，天下潰叛而不得聞；

translations.literal: The Second Emperor of Qin hid himself away and trusted Zhao Gao; the realm collapsed in rebellion and he could not hear of it;
translations.idiomatic: The Second Emperor of Qin shut himself away and put his trust in Zhao Gao; rebellion spread across the empire, yet he heard nothing of it;

sentences.zh: 梁武帝信硃異，侯景向關而不得聞；

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang trusted Zhu Yi; Hou Jing marched on the capital and he could not hear of it;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang trusted Zhu Yi; Hou Jing marched on the capital, yet he heard nothing of it;

sentences.zh: 隋煬帝信虞世基，賊遍天下而不得聞。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang of Sui trusted Yu Shiji; bandits spread throughout the realm and he could not hear of it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang of Sui trusted Yu Shiji; rebels spread across the empire, yet he heard nothing of it.

sentences.zh: 故曰，君能兼聽，則奸人不得壅蔽，而下情通矣。

translations.literal: Therefore it is said: if a ruler can listen broadly, then wicked men cannot obstruct and conceal, and the sentiments of those below will reach him.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the saying: when a ruler listens broadly, the wicked cannot block or conceal the truth, and the concerns of those below reach the throne.

sentences.zh: 鄭仁基息女美而才，皇后建請為充華，典冊具。

translations.literal: The daughter of Zheng Renji's son was beautiful and talented; the Empress repeatedly requested that she be made a Lady of Handsome Fairness, and the ceremonial documents were prepared.
translations.idiomatic: The daughter of Zheng Renji's son was both beautiful and gifted. The empress repeatedly asked that she be made a Lady of Handsome Fairness, and the investiture documents were already prepared.

sentences.zh: 或言許聘矣。

translations.literal: Someone said she had already been betrothed.
translations.idiomatic: Word came that she had already been promised in marriage.

sentences.zh: 徵諫曰：「陛下處台榭，則欲民有楝宇；

translations.literal: Wei Zheng remonstrated, saying: "When Your Majesty dwells in terraces and pavilions, you wish the people to have houses and roofs;
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng remonstrated: "When Your Majesty lives in palaces and pavilions, you wish the people to have homes of their own;

sentences.zh: 食膏粱，則欲民有飽適；

translations.literal: when you eat fine grains, you wish the people to be full and content;
translations.idiomatic: when you eat fine food, you wish the people to eat their fill;

sentences.zh: 顧嬪禦，則欲民有室家。

translations.literal: when you look upon palace ladies, you wish the people to have wives and families.
translations.idiomatic: when you choose consorts for the palace, you wish the people to have wives and families of their own.

sentences.zh: 今鄭已約昏，陛下取之，豈為人父母意！

translations.literal: Now the Zheng family has already arranged a marriage—if Your Majesty takes her, is this the mind of one who is a parent to the people!"
translations.idiomatic: The Zheng family has already arranged her marriage. If Your Majesty takes her anyway, is that the conduct of a ruler who acts as parent to the people?"

sentences.zh: 」帝痛自咎，即詔停冊。

translations.literal: " The Emperor deeply blamed himself and immediately issued an edict halting the investiture.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was deeply ashamed and at once issued an edict canceling the investiture.

sentences.zh: 貞觀三年，以秘書監參豫朝政。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenguan, as Director of the Palace Library he participated in deliberating court affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhenguan, as Director of the Palace Library he took part in deliberating court affairs.

sentences.zh: 高昌王曲文泰將入朝，西域諸國欲因文泰悉遣使者奉獻。

translations.literal: The King of Gaochang, Qu Wentai, was about to come to court, and the various states of the Western Regions wished to take advantage of Wentai's visit to send envoys bearing tribute.
translations.idiomatic: When the King of Gaochang, Qu Wentai, was about to come to court, the various states of the Western Regions all wanted to send envoys bearing tribute along with him.

sentences.zh: 帝詔文泰使人厭怛紇幹迎之。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Wentai's envoys to be met and escorted at Yandan Qagan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered that Wentai's envoys be met and escorted at Yandan Qagan.

sentences.zh: 徵曰：「異時文泰入朝，所過供擬不能具，今又加諸國焉，則瀕塞州縣以乏致罪者眾。

translations.literal: Wei Zheng said: "When Wentai came to court on a previous occasion, the supplies provided along the route could not be made adequate; now with the addition of envoys from all these states, many border prefectures and counties will be punished for shortages."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng said, "When Wentai came to court before, the localities along the route could not even supply his party adequately. Now, with envoys from all these states added, countless border counties will be punished for failing to meet the demand."

sentences.zh: 彼以商賈來，則邊人為之利；

translations.literal: If they come as merchants, then the border people will profit;
translations.idiomatic: If they come as traders, the border people will benefit;

sentences.zh: 若賓客之，中國蕭然耗矣。

translations.literal: if they are received as guests of honor, the heartland will be drained to exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: but if they are received as state guests, the heartland will be drained dry.

sentences.zh: 漢建武時，西域請置都護、送侍子，光武不許，不以蠻夷敝中國也。

translations.literal: In the Jianwu era of Han, the Western Regions requested the establishment of a Protectorate and the sending of hostage princes; Emperor Guangwu did not permit it, unwilling to let barbarian peoples exhaust China."
translations.idiomatic: In the Jianwu era of Han, the Western Regions asked to establish a Protectorate and send hostage princes; Emperor Guangwu refused, unwilling to let frontier peoples drain the resources of China."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「善。

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "Well said."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Well put."

sentences.zh: 」追止其詔。

translations.literal: " He recalled and halted the edict.
translations.idiomatic: " He revoked the edict.

sentences.zh: 於是帝即位四年，歲斷死二十九，幾至刑措，米斗三錢。

translations.literal: Thus in the fourth year of the Emperor's reign, only twenty-nine death sentences were passed for the year, punishments were nearly set aside altogether, and rice cost three cash per dou.
translations.idiomatic: By the fourth year of his reign, only twenty-nine death sentences were passed that year, punishments were all but abolished, and rice sold for three cash per dou.

sentences.zh: 先是，帝嘗歎曰：「今大亂之後，其難治乎？

translations.literal: Earlier the Emperor had once sighed and said: "After great chaos like this, will it not be hard to govern?"
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the emperor had sighed and said, "After such great upheaval, will the realm not be hard to govern?"

sentences.zh: 」徵曰：「大亂之易治，譬饑人之易食也。

translations.literal: " Wei Zheng said: "That great chaos makes governance easy is like a hungry man's ease in eating."
translations.idiomatic: " Wei Zheng replied, "That chaos makes governance easier is like hunger making food easier to eat."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「古不雲善人為邦百年，然後勝殘去殺邪？

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "Did the ancients not say that when a good man governs a state for a hundred years, only then are the violent overcome and killing abolished?"
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Did the ancients not say that only after a good man has governed a state for a hundred years are the violent overcome and executions abolished?"

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「此不為聖哲論也。

translations.literal: " He replied: "That is not a saying meant for sage rulers."
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "That saying was not meant for sage rulers."

sentences.zh: 聖哲之治，其應如響，期月而可，蓋不其難。

translations.literal: The governance of sage rulers responds like an echo; within a month or a year it can be achieved—it is not so difficult.
translations.idiomatic: The rule of a sage responds like an echo; within a month or a year it can be achieved. It is not so difficult as people imagine.

sentences.zh: 」封德彝曰：「不然。

translations.literal: " Feng Deyi said: "Not so."
translations.idiomatic: " Feng Deyi objected, "Not so."

sentences.zh: 三代之後，澆詭日滋。

translations.literal: After the Three Dynasties, depravity and cunning grew daily.
translations.idiomatic: After the Three Dynasties, depravity and cunning grew worse with each passing day.

sentences.zh: 秦任法律，漢雜霸道，皆欲治不能，非能治不欲。

translations.literal: Qin relied on law, Han mixed in hegemonic rule—both wanted to govern but could not; it was not that they could govern but did not wish to.
translations.idiomatic: Qin relied on law, Han mixed in hegemonic methods—both wanted to govern well but could not. It was not that they could govern but chose not to.

sentences.zh: 徵書生，好虛論，徒亂國家，不可聽。

translations.literal: Wei Zheng is a bookish scholar who loves empty talk; he will only disorder the state and should not be heeded."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng is a bookish pedant who loves idle theorizing. He will only throw the state into confusion and should not be listened to."

sentences.zh: 」徵曰：「五帝、三王不易民以教，行帝道而帝，行王道而王，顧所行何如爾。

translations.literal: " Wei Zheng said: "The Five Emperors and Three Kings did not change the people in order to teach them; they practiced the Way of the Emperor and became emperors, practiced the Kingly Way and became kings—it all depended on what path they followed."
translations.idiomatic: " Wei Zheng replied, "The Five Emperors and Three Kings did not change the people in order to teach them. They practiced the Way of the Emperor and became emperors; they practiced the Kingly Way and became kings. Everything depended on the path they chose."

sentences.zh: 黃帝逐蚩尤，七十戰而勝其亂，因致無為。

translations.literal: The Yellow Emperor drove out Chiyou; after seventy battles he overcame the chaos and thereby achieved non-action.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Emperor drove out Chiyou. After seventy battles he quelled the chaos and thereby achieved effortless rule.

sentences.zh: 九黎害德，顓頊征之，已克而治。

translations.literal: The Nine Li harmed virtue; Zhuanxu campaigned against them, and once he had conquered them, he governed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Nine Li threatened moral order, Zhuanxu campaigned against them and, once they were subdued, brought order to the realm.

sentences.zh: 桀為亂，湯放之；

translations.literal: Jie brought chaos, and Tang banished him;
translations.idiomatic: Jie brought chaos, and Tang banished him;

sentences.zh: 紂無道，武王伐之。

translations.literal: Zhou was without the Way, and King Wu attacked him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou was without the Way, and King Wu attacked him.

sentences.zh: 湯、武身及太平。

translations.literal: Tang and Wu themselves lived to see great peace.
translations.idiomatic: Tang and Wu themselves lived to see an age of great peace.

sentences.zh: 若人漸澆詭，不復返樸，今當為鬼為魅，尚安得而化哉！

translations.literal: If people gradually grow depraved and cunning and no longer return to simplicity, then even if one were a ghost or demon, how could one transform them!"
translations.idiomatic: If people grow ever more depraved and cunning and no longer return to simplicity, then even if one were a ghost or demon, how could one transform them!"

sentences.zh: 」德彝不能對，然心以為不可。

translations.literal: " Deyi could not reply, but in his heart he still thought it could not be so.
translations.idiomatic: " Deyi had no answer, though in his heart he still did not believe it.

sentences.zh: 帝納之不疑。

translations.literal: The Emperor accepted it without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted Wei Zheng's view without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 至是，天下大治。

translations.literal: By this time the realm was greatly well governed.
translations.idiomatic: By this time the realm was at peace and well governed.

sentences.zh: 蠻夷君長襲衣冠，帶刀宿衛。

translations.literal: Barbarian chieftains donned Chinese robes and caps and served as armed guards at the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarian chieftains donned Chinese robes and caps and served as armed guards at the palace.

sentences.zh: 東薄海，南逾嶺，戶闔不閉，行旅不齎糧，取給於道。

translations.literal: To the east the realm reached the sea; to the south it crossed the mountains. Household doors were left unbarred, travelers carried no provisions, and took what they needed along the road.
translations.idiomatic: The realm stretched east to the sea and south beyond the mountains. People left their doors unbarred, travelers carried no provisions, and found what they needed along the road.

sentences.zh: 帝謂群臣曰：「此徵勸我行仁義，既效矣。

translations.literal: The Emperor said to the assembled ministers: "This is because Wei Zheng urged me to practice benevolence and righteousness—it has already taken effect.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told his ministers, "This is because Wei Zheng urged me to practice benevolence and righteousness—and it has already borne fruit.

sentences.zh: 惜不令封德彝見之！

translations.literal: It is a pity that Feng Deyi was not made to see this!"
translations.idiomatic: It is a pity Feng Deyi is not here to see it!"

sentences.zh: 俄檢校侍中，進爵郡公。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was made Acting Palace Attendant and advanced in rank to Duke of the Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made Acting Palace Attendant and promoted to Duke of the Commandery.

sentences.zh: 帝幸九成宮，宮禦舍湋川宮下。

translations.literal: The Emperor visited Jiucheng Palace; the palace women were lodged below Weichuan Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor visited Jiucheng Palace, and the palace women were quartered at Weichuan Palace below.

sentences.zh: 僕射李靖、侍中王珪繼至，吏改館宮禦以舍靖、珪。

translations.literal: Left Pushe Li Jing and Palace Attendant Wang Gui arrived in succession; the officials changed the lodgings of the palace women to house Jing and Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Left Pushe Li Jing and Palace Attendant Wang Gui arrived shortly afterward, and the officials reallocated the palace women's quarters to lodge Jing and Gui.

sentences.zh: 帝聞，怒曰：「威福由是等邪！

translations.literal: The Emperor heard and said in anger: "Are authority and favor to be wielded by such people!
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of it, he said in anger, "Is authority and favor to be wielded by people like this!

sentences.zh: 何輕我宮人？

translations.literal: Why do you slight my palace women?
translations.idiomatic: Why do you treat my palace women so lightly?

sentences.zh: 」詔並按之。

translations.literal: " He ordered them all to be investigated.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered them all prosecuted.

sentences.zh: 徵曰：「靖、珪皆陛下腹心大臣，宮人止後宮掃除隸耳。

translations.literal: Wei Zheng said: "Jing and Gui are both trusted ministers at Your Majesty's heart; palace women are merely attendants of the inner quarters for sweeping and cleaning.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng said, "Jing and Gui are both trusted ministers close to Your Majesty's heart; palace women are only attendants of the inner quarters who sweep and clean.

sentences.zh: 方大臣出，官吏諮朝廷法式；

translations.literal: When grand ministers go out, officials consult them on court laws and regulations;
translations.idiomatic: When great ministers leave on business, officials consult them on court regulations and statutes;

sentences.zh: 歸來，陛下問人間疾苦。

translations.literal: When they return, Your Majesty asks about the people's hardships.
translations.idiomatic: When they return, Your Majesty inquires about the people's suffering.

sentences.zh: 夫官舍，固靖等見官吏之所，吏不可不謁也。

translations.literal: As for official lodging, it is naturally where Jing and the others receive officials; officials cannot fail to pay their respects.
translations.idiomatic: Official lodgings are naturally where Jing and the others receive officials—officials cannot fail to pay their respects.

sentences.zh: 至宮人則不然，供饋之餘無所參承。

translations.literal: As for palace women, it is not so; beyond supplying provisions there is no business of consultation or audience.
translations.idiomatic: Palace women are another matter: beyond supplying food, they have no duties of consultation or audience.

sentences.zh: 以此按吏，且駭天下耳目。

translations.literal: To investigate officials on this account would moreover shock the ears and eyes of all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: To prosecute the officials over this would shock the whole realm.

sentences.zh: 」帝悟，寢不問。

translations.literal: " The Emperor understood and let the matter drop without further inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor came to his senses and dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 後宴丹霄樓，酒中謂長孫無忌曰：「魏徵、王珪事隱太子、巢刺王時，誠可惡，我能棄怨用才，無羞古人。

translations.literal: Later, at a banquet in Danxiao Tower, mid-cups he said to Zhangsun Wuji: "When Wei Zheng and Wang Gui served the Hidden Crown Prince and the Prince of Qi, they were indeed detestable; I can set aside resentment and employ talent—I need not blush before the ancients.
translations.idiomatic: Later, while feasting at Danxiao Tower, the emperor said mid-cups to Zhangsun Wuji, "When Wei Zheng and Wang Gui served the Hidden Crown Prince and the Prince of Qi, they were truly odious—but I can put aside old resentments and employ talent. I need not blush before the ancients.

sentences.zh: 然徵每諫我不從，我發言輒不即應，何哉？

translations.literal: Yet whenever Zheng remonstrates and I do not follow, whenever I speak he does not immediately respond—why is that?
translations.idiomatic: Yet whenever Zheng remonstrates with me and I do not heed him, he never answers me immediately when I speak. Why is that?

sentences.zh: 」徵曰：「臣以事有不可，故諫，若不從輒應，恐遂行之。

translations.literal: " Wei Zheng said: "Your servant, because matters may be impermissible, therefore remonstrates; if when not followed one immediately assents, I fear they will then be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: " Wei Zheng replied, "Your servant remonstrates because some matters ought not be done. If I assented the moment You did not heed me, I fear they would then be carried out.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「弟即應，須別陳論，顧不得？

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "You may assent at once, then separately set forth your argument—can you not?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "You could assent at once and then set forth a separate argument—would that not do?

sentences.zh: 」徵曰：「昔舜戒群臣：'爾無面從，退有後言。

translations.literal: " Wei Zheng said: "In antiquity Shun warned his ministers: 'Do not obey to one's face and speak behind one's back afterward.
translations.idiomatic: " Wei Zheng said, "Long ago Shun warned his ministers, 'Do not obey to one's face and speak differently behind one's back.

sentences.zh: '若面從可，方別陳論，此乃後言，非稷、蒐所以事堯、舜也。

translations.literal: 'If obeying to the face were permissible, then setting forth a separate argument afterward would be speaking behind the back; this is not how Hou Ji and Xie served Yao and Shun.
translations.idiomatic: 'If assenting to one's face were acceptable, then offering a separate argument afterward would itself be speaking behind one's back. That is not how Hou Ji and Xie served Yao and Shun.

sentences.zh: 」帝大笑曰：「人言徵舉動疏慢，我但見其嫵媚耳！

translations.literal: " The Emperor laughed greatly and said: "People say Zheng in bearing is negligent and rude, but I only see his ingratiating grace!
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor burst out laughing and said, "People say Zheng's bearing is careless and insolent—but I see only his charming persuasiveness!

sentences.zh: 」徵再拜曰：「陛下導臣使言，所以敢然；

translations.literal: " Wei Zheng bowed again and said: "Your Majesty guides your servant to speak; therefore I dare do so;
translations.idiomatic: " Wei Zheng bowed again and said, "Your Majesty encourages your servant to speak—that is why I dare speak so frankly;

sentences.zh: 若不受，臣敢數批逆鱗哉！

translations.literal: If not received, how would your servant dare repeatedly to touch the inverted scales!
translations.idiomatic: If You did not welcome it, how would your servant dare repeatedly to touch the dragon's scales against the grain!

sentences.zh: 十年，為侍中。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, he was made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, he was made Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 尚書省滯訟不決者，詔徵平治。

translations.literal: For lawsuits stalled and undecided in the Ministry of State, an edict ordered Zheng to settle and resolve them.
translations.idiomatic: Lawsuits stalled in the Ministry of State were ordered settled by Wei Zheng.

sentences.zh: 徵不素習法，但存大體，處事以情，人人悅服。

translations.literal: Zheng was not by nature versed in law, but preserved the great framework, handled matters according to human feelings, and everyone was pleased and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng was not trained in law, but he upheld the broad principles and judged cases with human sympathy—everyone was satisfied.

sentences.zh: 進左光祿大夫、鄭國公。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Duke of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Duke of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 多病，辭職，帝曰：「公獨不見金在鑛何足貴邪？

translations.literal: Often ill, he resigned his office; the Emperor said: "Sir, do you alone not see that gold in the ore is nothing worth valuing?
translations.idiomatic: He fell frequently ill and asked to resign. The emperor said, "Do you not see that raw gold in the mine is worth nothing?

sentences.zh: 善冶鍛而為器，人乃寶之。

translations.literal: When skillfully smelted and forged into utensils, people then treasure it.
translations.idiomatic: Only when skillfully refined and forged into a vessel do people treasure it.

sentences.zh: 朕方自比于金，以卿為良匠而加礪焉。

translations.literal: I am now comparing myself to gold, and take you as a fine craftsman to sharpen and polish me.
translations.idiomatic: I compare myself to gold and take you as a fine craftsman to sharpen and polish me.

sentences.zh: 卿雖疾，未及衰，庸得便爾？

translations.literal: Though you are ill, you have not yet reached decline—how can you leave so readily?
translations.idiomatic: You are ill, but not yet in decline—how can you leave so easily?

sentences.zh: 」徵懇請，數卻愈牢。

translations.literal: " Zheng pleaded earnestly; each refusal grew firmer.
translations.idiomatic: " Wei Zheng pleaded earnestly, but the more he was refused, the more firmly he pressed his request.

sentences.zh: 乃拜特進，知門下省事，詔朝章國典，參議得失，祿賜、國官、防閤並同職事。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was appointed Special Grand Master and placed in charge of Chancellery affairs; by edict he was to participate in deliberating the gains and losses of court regulations and state institutions, and salary gifts, state appointees, and guards were all the same as for an incumbent official.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he was appointed Special Grand Master and placed in charge of Chancellery affairs, with orders to deliberate court regulations and state institutions and comment on their strengths and flaws; his salary, gifts, household staff, and guards were all on the same footing as an incumbent minister.

sentences.zh: 文德皇后既葬，帝即苑中作層觀，以望昭陵，引徵同升，徵孰視曰：「臣眊昏，不能見。

translations.literal: After Empress Wende was buried, the Emperor immediately built a multi-storied tower in the park to gaze upon Zhao Mausoleum; he brought Zheng to ascend with him. Zheng stared intently and said: "Your servant's eyes are dim and failing; I cannot see.
translations.idiomatic: After Empress Wende was buried, the emperor built a multi-storied tower in the park to gaze upon Zhao Mausoleum and had Wei Zheng ascend with him. Wei Zheng looked closely and said, "Your servant's eyes are dim—I cannot see.

sentences.zh: 」帝指示之，徵曰：「此昭陵邪？

translations.literal: " The Emperor pointed it out to him. Zheng said: "Is this Zhao Mausoleum?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor pointed it out. Wei Zheng said, "Is this Zhao Mausoleum?

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「然。

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "It is.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "It is.

sentences.zh: 」徵曰：「臣以為陛下望獻陵，若昭陵，臣固見之。

translations.literal: " Zheng said: "Your servant thought Your Majesty was gazing at Xian Mausoleum; if it were Zhao Mausoleum, I would certainly see it.
translations.idiomatic: " Wei Zheng said, "Your servant thought Your Majesty was looking toward Xian Mausoleum. If it were Zhao Mausoleum, I would surely have seen it.

sentences.zh: 」帝泣，為毀觀。

translations.literal: " The Emperor wept and had the tower destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor wept and had the tower torn down.

sentences.zh: 尋以定五禮，當封一子縣男，徵請封孤兄子叔慈。

translations.literal: Soon, on account of fixing the Five Rites, he was to ennoble one son as Baron of a county; Zheng requested that the title go to his orphaned elder brother's son Shuci.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, for his role in codifying the Five Rites, he was entitled to ennoble one son as a county baron. Wei Zheng asked instead to ennoble his late elder brother's orphaned son Shuci.

sentences.zh: 帝愴然曰：「此可以勵俗。

translations.literal: The Emperor said mournfully: "This can inspire custom.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, deeply moved, "This can inspire the people.

sentences.zh: 」即許之。

translations.literal: " He immediately granted it.
translations.idiomatic: " He granted it at once.

sentences.zh: 後幸洛陽，次昭仁宮，多所譴責。

translations.literal: Later the Emperor visited Luoyang and stopped at Zhaoren Palace, issuing many reprimands and reproaches.
translations.idiomatic: Later the emperor visited Luoyang and lodged at Zhaoren Palace, where he issued many reprimands.

sentences.zh: 徵曰：「隋惟責不獻食，或供奉不精，為此無限，而至於亡。

translations.literal: Wei Zheng said: "The Sui only reproached people for not presenting food or for imprecise tribute; on this account there was no limit, and the dynasty came to ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng said, "The Sui dynasty condemned people only for failing to present food or for substandard tribute. Such demands knew no bounds—and led to the dynasty's fall.

sentences.zh: 故天命陛下代之，正當兢懼戒約，奈何令人悔為不奢。

translations.literal: Therefore Heaven's mandate replaced them with Your Majesty; one should just be vigilant, fearful, and restrained—how can one make people regret not being extravagant?
translations.idiomatic: Heaven therefore entrusted the realm to Your Majesty in their place. You ought to be vigilant, restrained, and wary. How can you make people regret that they were not more extravagant?

sentences.zh: 若以為足，今不啻足矣；

translations.literal: If you deem it sufficient, what exists now is more than sufficient;
translations.idiomatic: If you deem this enough, what you have now is more than enough;

sentences.zh: 以為不足，萬此寧有足邪？

translations.literal: If you deem it insufficient, even ten thousand times this, how could there be enough?
translations.idiomatic: If you deem it insufficient, even ten thousand times as much would never be enough.

sentences.zh: 」帝驚曰：「非公不聞此言。

translations.literal: " The Emperor said in alarm: "Were it not for you, I would not have heard these words.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, startled, "If not for you, I would never have heard such words.

sentences.zh: 」退又上疏曰：

translations.literal: " After withdrawing, he again submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: " Afterward Wei Zheng submitted another memorial, saying:

sentences.zh: 《書》稱「明德慎罰」，「惟刑之恤」。

translations.literal: The Documents says: "Illustrate virtue and be cautious in punishments," "be compassionate in the use of punishments."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents says, "Illustrate virtue and be cautious in punishment," and "be compassionate in administering punishments."

sentences.zh: 《禮》曰：「為上易事，為下易知，則刑不煩。

translations.literal: The Rites says: "For superiors make affairs easy, for inferiors make things easy to know, then punishments are not numerous.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Rites says, "When superiors find their tasks easy and inferiors easy to understand, punishments need not be numerous.

sentences.zh: 」「上多疑，則百姓惑；

translations.literal: " "When superiors are much doubting, the common people are perplexed;
translations.idiomatic: " "When the ruler is overly suspicious, the people grow confused;

sentences.zh: 下難知，則君長勞。

translations.literal: If those below are hard to know, then the lord and superiors will be wearied.
translations.idiomatic: When inferiors are difficult to fathom, rulers and chiefs exhaust themselves.

sentences.zh: 」夫上易事，下易知，君長不勞，百姓不惑，故君有一德，臣無二心。

translations.literal: Thus, when those above are easy to serve and those below are easy to know, lords need not toil and the common people are not confused—therefore the sovereign holds to one virtue and ministers have no second heart.
translations.idiomatic: When superiors are easy to serve and inferiors easy to understand, rulers need not wear themselves out and the people need not be bewildered. Then the sovereign keeps to a single standard, and his ministers harbor no divided loyalty.

sentences.zh: 夫刑賞之本，在乎勸善而懲惡。

translations.literal: The root of punishments and rewards lies in encouraging goodness and punishing evil.
translations.idiomatic: Punishment and reward exist above all to promote virtue and chastise wrongdoing.

sentences.zh: 帝王所與，天下畫一，不以親疏貴賤而輕重者也。

translations.literal: What emperors and kings bestow should be uniform throughout the realm, not weighted according to closeness or distance, nobility or baseness.
translations.idiomatic: What a sovereign grants must be one law for all under Heaven, never lighter or heavier for kin or stranger, for the highborn or the low.

sentences.zh: 今之刑賞，或由喜怒，或出好惡。

translations.literal: Today's punishments and rewards sometimes follow joy and anger, sometimes arise from likes and dislikes.
translations.idiomatic: Punishments and rewards now are meted out at whim—now by mood, now by personal favor or disfavor.

sentences.zh: 喜則矜刑於法中，怒則求罪於律外；

translations.literal: When pleased, one spares punishment within the law; when angry, one seeks guilt outside the law.
translations.idiomatic: In pleasure, the law is stretched to show mercy; in anger, guilt is hunted beyond what the statutes allow.

sentences.zh: 好則鑽皮出羽，惡則洗垢索瘢。

translations.literal: When one favors someone, one splits the hide to find a feather; when one hates someone, one scrubs away filth to seek a scar.
translations.idiomatic: For those favored, the skin is picked apart to discover merit; for those despised, every stain is scrubbed until a blemish appears.

sentences.zh: 蓋刑濫則小人道長，賞謬則君子道消。

translations.literal: For when punishments are abused, the way of petty men grows long; when rewards are mistaken, the way of gentlemen is extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: When punishment runs wild, the petty flourish; when reward goes astray, the upright are driven from the path.

sentences.zh: 小人之惡不懲，君子之善不勸，而望治安刑措，非所聞也。

translations.literal: If the evil of petty men is not punished and the goodness of gentlemen is not encouraged, yet one hopes for peace and the laying aside of punishments—this is not something I have heard of.
translations.idiomatic: If the wicked go unchecked and the worthy unrewarded, yet one still expects tranquillity and the abolition of the penal code—I have never heard of such a thing.

sentences.zh: 且暇豫而言，皆敦尚孔、老；

translations.literal: Moreover, in leisure and ease they speak, and all honor Confucius and Laozi.
translations.idiomatic: In moments of ease they speak only of revering Confucius and Laozi.

sentences.zh: 至於威怒，則專法申、韓。

translations.literal: But when stern anger comes, they apply exclusively the law of Shen and Han.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when wrath rises, they govern by nothing but the harsh doctrines of Shen Buhai and Han Fei.

sentences.zh: 故道德之旨未弘，而鍥薄之風先搖。

translations.literal: Thus the intent of moral virtue is not yet broadly spread, while the wind of shallow parsimony already stirs.
translations.idiomatic: The spirit of virtue has scarcely taken root, while the taste for harsh severity already blows through the court.

sentences.zh: 昔州犁上下其手而楚法以敝，張湯輕重其心而漢刑以謬，況人主而自高下乎！

translations.literal: In the past Yang Chu tipped the scales with his hand and Chu law was ruined; Zhang Tang weighed heavy and light by his own heart and Han punishments went astray—how much more when the ruler himself sets the weights high and low!
translations.idiomatic: Of old, Yang Chu rigged the balance and Chu law collapsed; Zhang Tang bent the scales to his whim and Han justice went awry—what then when the Son of Heaven himself raises and lowers the weights?

sentences.zh: 頃者罰人，或以供張不贍，或不能從欲，皆非致治之急也。

translations.literal: Recently people have been punished sometimes for insufficient provisioning at banquets, sometimes for failing to satisfy desires—none of these are urgent to bringing about good governance.
translations.idiomatic: Lately men have been punished for inadequate feasts, or for failing to gratify every wish—matters far removed from the urgent business of good rule.

sentences.zh: 夫貴不與驕期而驕自至，富不與奢期而奢自至，非徒語也。

translations.literal: Nobility does not arrange with arrogance, yet arrogance comes of itself; wealth does not arrange with extravagance, yet extravagance comes of itself—this is no empty saying.
translations.idiomatic: Rank needs no appointment with pride for pride to arrive; riches need no tryst with extravagance for extravagance to follow—this is no idle proverb.

sentences.zh: 且我之所代，實在有隋。

translations.literal: Moreover, the dynasty we have replaced is indeed the Sui.
translations.idiomatic: The realm we now hold is the very one we took from the Sui.

sentences.zh: 以隋府藏況今之資儲，以隋甲兵況今之士馬，以隋戶口況今之百姓，挈長度大，曾何等級焉！

translations.literal: Compare the Sui treasury with today's stores, Sui armor and weapons with today's troops and horses, Sui population with today's common people—taking the long to measure the short: how could they be equal in rank!
translations.idiomatic: Set the Sui treasuries beside our stores today, their arms and armor beside our soldiers and horses, their registered households beside our people—measure the greater against the lesser, and we are not even of the same order!

sentences.zh: 然隋以富強而喪，動之也；

translations.literal: Yet the Sui perished though rich and strong—because it was stirred into motion.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Sui, for all its wealth and might, was destroyed—because it would not keep still.

sentences.zh: 我以貧寡而安，靜之也。

translations.literal: We are secure in poverty and fewness—because we keep still.
translations.idiomatic: We remain secure in our poverty and smallness—because we hold ourselves in quiet.

sentences.zh: 靜之則安，動之則亂，人皆知之，非隱而難見、微而難察也。

translations.literal: Stillness brings security; motion brings chaos—all know this. It is not hidden and hard to see, subtle and hard to perceive.
translations.idiomatic: Quiet brings peace; unrest brings disorder—everyone knows this. It is neither hidden from sight nor too fine to discern.

sentences.zh: 不蹈平易之塗，而遵覆車之轍，何哉？

translations.literal: Why not tread the level, easy road, but follow the ruts of overturned chariots?
translations.idiomatic: Why leave the broad, level path to follow the tracks of a wrecked cart?

sentences.zh: 安不思危，治不念亂，存不慮亡也。

translations.literal: In security one does not think of danger; in order one does not remember chaos; in survival one does not consider destruction.
translations.idiomatic: Secure, one forgets peril; well governed, one forgets disorder; while the state stands, one forgets how it may fall.

sentences.zh: 方隋未亂，自謂必無亂；

translations.literal: When the Sui had not yet fallen into chaos, they assured themselves there would surely be no chaos.
translations.idiomatic: Before the Sui unraveled, they were certain it never would.

sentences.zh: 未亡，自謂必不亡。

translations.literal: Before they perished, they assured themselves they would surely not perish.
translations.idiomatic: Before they were destroyed, they were certain they never could be.

sentences.zh: 所以甲兵亟動，徭役不息，以至戮辱而不悟滅亡之所由也，豈不哀哉！

translations.literal: Therefore armor and weapons were constantly deployed, corvée labor never ceased, until disgrace and ruin—and still they did not perceive the source of their destruction. How lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: So arms were ever on the march and forced labor never rested, until shame and ruin overtook them—yet still they did not see what brought their fall. Is it not pitiful!

sentences.zh: 夫監形之美惡，必就止水；

translations.literal: To inspect the beauty or ugliness of form, one must go to still water.
translations.idiomatic: To judge whether a face is fair or foul, one must look into calm water.

sentences.zh: 監'政之安危，必取亡國。

translations.literal: To observe the safety or danger of governance, one must take a perished state as mirror.
translations.idiomatic: To gauge whether rule is secure or imperiled, one must take a fallen kingdom as one's mirror.

sentences.zh: 《詩》曰：「殷鑒不遠，在夏後之世。

translations.literal: The Classic of Poetry says: "Yin's mirror is not far—it is in the age of Xia's successor."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Songs says: "The mirror of Yin is not distant—it lies in the age that followed Xia."

sentences.zh: 臣願當今之動靜，以隋為鑒，則存亡治亂可得而知。

translations.literal: Your servant hopes that in today's actions and stillness, taking the Sui as mirror, survival and destruction, order and chaos may be known beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty, in every move and every pause of the present reign, to take the Sui as warning—then whether the state will stand or fall, govern well or sink into chaos, may be foreseen.

sentences.zh: 思所以危則安矣，思所以亂則治矣，思所以亡則存矣。

translations.literal: Think on what brings danger and you will be secure; think on what brings chaos and you will have order; think on what brings destruction and you will survive.
translations.idiomatic: Reflect on the causes of peril and you will remain safe; reflect on the causes of disorder and you will keep the realm governed; reflect on the causes of ruin and you will preserve the state.

sentences.zh: 存亡之所在，在節嗜欲，省遊畋，息靡麗，罷不急，慎偏聽，近忠厚，遠便佞而已。

translations.literal: Where survival and destruction lie is simply in restraining appetites, reducing hunting excursions, ending extravagance, abolishing what is not urgent, being cautious of partial listening, drawing near to loyalty and good faith, and keeping distant from glib flatterers.
translations.idiomatic: Whether the state endures or perishes depends on nothing more than curbing desire, cutting back the hunt, laying aside splendor, dropping what is not urgent, guarding against one-sided counsel, cleaving to loyalty and sincerity, and keeping glib sycophants at a distance.

sentences.zh: 夫守之則易，得之實難。

translations.literal: To keep it is easy; to obtain it was truly hard.
translations.idiomatic: What is won with difficulty is kept with ease—or so it should be.

sentences.zh: 今既得其所難，豈不能保其所易？

translations.literal: Now having already attained what was difficult, can you not preserve what is easy?
translations.idiomatic: Having already gained what was hard to gain, can you not guard what is easy to keep?

sentences.zh: 保之不固，驕奢淫泆有以動之也。

translations.literal: If you do not hold it firm, arrogance, extravagance, and dissoluteness will have means to stir it into motion.
translations.idiomatic: Fail to hold it fast, and pride, luxury, and excess will set it moving again.

sentences.zh: 帝宴群臣積翠池，酣樂賦詩。

translations.literal: The Emperor feasted his ministers at Jicui Pool, reveling in pleasure and composing poetry.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave a banquet for his ministers at the Pool of Accumulated Emerald, drinking deep in merriment and composing verses.

sentences.zh: 徵賦《西漢》，其卒章曰：「終藉叔孫禮，方知皇帝尊。

translations.literal: Zheng recited "Western Han"; its final stanza says: "Only by relying on Shusun Tong's rites does one know the Emperor's dignity."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng recited his poem "Western Han," whose closing lines run: "Only through Shusun Tong's rites does one learn how august an emperor truly is."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「徵言未嘗不約我以禮。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Zheng's words never fail to bind me with ritual propriety."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Never once has Zheng spoken without schooling me in propriety."

sentences.zh: 」它日，從容問曰：「比政治若何？

translations.literal: Another day, at leisure he asked: "How is governance lately?"
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion, speaking at ease, he asked, "How stands the realm's governance of late?"

sentences.zh: 」徵見久承平，帝意有所忽，因對曰：「陛下貞觀之初，導人使諫。

translations.literal: Zheng, seeing long peace and that the Emperor's mind was somewhat neglectful, replied: "Your Majesty, at the beginning of the Zhenguan era, you guided people to remonstrate.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng, seeing how long peace had lasted and that the emperor's attention had grown lax, answered, "At the opening of the Zhenguan reign, Your Majesty encouraged men to speak plainly.

sentences.zh: 三年以後，見諫者悅而從之。

translations.literal: Three years later, when you saw remonstrators you were pleased and followed them.
translations.idiomatic: After three years, when remonstrance came you took it gladly and acted on it.

sentences.zh: 比一二年，勉強受諫，而終不平也。

translations.literal: In the last year or two, you reluctantly accept remonstrance, yet in the end remain displeased.
translations.idiomatic: These last one or two years, you accept counsel only with reluctance—and in your heart you are never quite at peace with it.

sentences.zh: 」帝驚曰：「公何物驗之？

translations.literal: The Emperor, startled, said: "Sir, by what do you verify this?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, taken aback, said, "On what grounds do you say so?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「陛下初即位，論元律師死，孫伏伽諫以為法不當死，陛下賜以蘭陵公主園，直百萬。

translations.literal: He replied: "When Your Majesty first ascended the throne, there was discussion of executing Lawyer Yuan; Sun Fugue remonstrated that the law did not warrant death, and Your Majesty granted him Princess Lanling's garden, worth a million."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "When Your Majesty first took the throne, the court debated putting Lawyer Yuan to death. Sun Fugue remonstrated that the law did not require death, and Your Majesty gave him Princess Lanling's estate, worth a million cash."

sentences.zh: 或曰：『賞太厚。

translations.literal: Someone said: 'The reward is too generous.'
translations.idiomatic: Someone said, 'The reward is too lavish.'

sentences.zh: 』答曰：『朕即位，未有諫者，所以賞之。

translations.literal: He answered: 'I have just ascended the throne and had no remonstrators yet—that is why I reward him.'
translations.idiomatic: You answered, 'I have only just come to the throne and had not yet heard a single remonstrance—that is why I rewarded him.'

sentences.zh: 』此導人使諫也。

translations.literal: This was guiding people to remonstrate.
translations.idiomatic: That was encouraging men to speak up.

sentences.zh: 後柳雄妄訴隋資，有司得，劾其偽，將論死，戴胄奏罪當徒，執之四五然後赦。

translations.literal: Later Liu Xiong falsely claimed Sui-era assets; the officials caught him, impeached him for fraud, and were about to sentence him to death; Dai Zhou memorialized that the crime warranted only exile; Your Majesty held to this four or five times before finally pardoning him.
translations.idiomatic: Later Liu Xiong falsely claimed assets from the Sui; the authorities caught him, charged him with fraud, and were about to condemn him to death. Dai Zhou submitted that the offense merited only penal servitude. Your Majesty held firm four or five times before granting pardon at last.

sentences.zh: 謂胄曰『弟守法如此，不畏濫罰。

translations.literal: You said to Zhou: 'Younger brother, you uphold the law like this—you fear not excessive punishment.'
translations.idiomatic: You told Dai Zhou, 'My friend, you hold to the law so steadfastly—you do not shrink from my overbearing punishments.'

sentences.zh: 』此悅而從諫也。

translations.literal: This was being pleased and following remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: That was taking remonstrance gladly and yielding to it.

sentences.zh: 近皇甫德參上書言『修洛陽宮，勞人也；

translations.literal: Recently Huangfu Dekcan submitted a memorial saying 'Repairing Luoyang Palace—it burdens the people;
translations.idiomatic: Not long ago Huangfu Dekcan submitted a memorial stating, 'The repairs to Luoyang Palace impose hardship on the people;

sentences.zh: 收地租，厚斂也；

translations.literal: Collecting land rent is heavy exaction;
translations.idiomatic: To levy land rents is to burden the people with heavy taxation;

sentences.zh: 俗尚高髻，宮中所化也。

translations.literal: The custom of favoring high topknots is what the palace has made fashionable.
translations.idiomatic: The vogue for towering coiffures—that is the palace's doing.

sentences.zh: 』陛下恚曰：『是子使國家不役一人，不收一租，宮人無髮，乃稱其意。

translations.literal: Your Majesty said in anger: 'This man would have the state conscript not a single man, collect not a single rent, and have palace women go without hair—only then would he call it meeting my wishes.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said in wrath, 'This fellow would have the realm press not one soul into service, take not one coin in rent, and leave the palace women without a single lock of hair—only then would he deem my wishes fulfilled.'

sentences.zh: 』臣奏：『人臣上書，不激切不能起人主意，激切即近訕謗。

translations.literal: The minister submitted: 'When a subject memorializes, unless he is forceful and cutting he cannot stir the ruler's mind; yet if he is forceful and cutting, he comes close to slander.'
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng replied, 'When a minister submits a memorial, he cannot rouse his sovereign's attention unless he speaks with sharp urgency—and yet sharp urgency borders on slander.'

sentences.zh: 』于時，陛下雖從臣言，賞帛罷之，意終不平。

translations.literal: At that time, though Your Majesty followed the minister's words, rewarded him with silk, and let the matter drop, in your heart you were never at peace.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, though Your Majesty took my counsel, rewarded me with silk, and dismissed the matter, your heart remained unsettled to the end.

sentences.zh: 此難於受諫也。

translations.literal: This is what makes accepting remonstrance difficult.
translations.idiomatic: This is why it is so hard for a ruler to accept honest counsel.

sentences.zh: 」帝悟曰：「非公，無能道此者。

translations.literal: The Emperor came to his senses and said: 'Were it not for you, none could speak thus.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw the truth and said, 'But for you, no one could have put it so plainly.

sentences.zh: 人苦不自覺耳！

translations.literal: People suffer because they do not know themselves!
translations.idiomatic: The trouble with men is that they cannot see themselves clearly!

sentences.zh: 先是，帝作飛仙宮，徵上疏曰：

translations.literal: Earlier, the Emperor had built the Flying Immortal Palace; Wei Zheng submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the emperor had raised the Flying Immortal Palace. Wei Zheng submitted a memorial, saying:

sentences.zh: 隋有天下三十餘年，風行萬里，威詹殊俗，一旦舉而棄之。

translations.literal: The Sui held the realm for more than thirty years; its influence spread ten thousand li; its might awed distant peoples—then in a single moment it was cast away entirely.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui ruled the realm for more than thirty years. Its influence reached ten thousand li; its might overawed foreign lands—and then, in a single stroke, it was cast aside.

sentences.zh: 彼煬帝者，豈惡治安、喜滅亡哉？

translations.literal: That Emperor Yang—did he hate good order and delight in ruin?
translations.idiomatic: Did Emperor Yang truly hate peace and love destruction?

sentences.zh: 恃其富強，不虞後患也。

translations.literal: He relied on his wealth and strength and did not guard against calamity to come.
translations.idiomatic: He trusted in his wealth and power, and gave no thought to the ruin that would follow.

sentences.zh: 驅天下，役萬物，以自奉養，子女玉帛是求，宮宇台榭是飾，徭役無時，干戈不休，外示威重，內行險忌，讒邪者進，忠正者退，上下相蒙，人不堪命，以致殞匹夫之手，為天下笑。

translations.literal: He drove all under Heaven, conscripted all things, to supply his own wants; he sought sons and daughters, jade and silk; he adorned himself with palaces, towers, and pavilions; corvée labor knew no season; arms were never stilled; outwardly he displayed might and majesty, inwardly he practiced treachery and jealousy; slanderers and the wicked advanced, the loyal and upright retreated; high and low deceived one another; the people could not bear their lot—until he perished at the hands of a common man and became the laughingstock of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He drove all under Heaven and pressed every living thing into his service. He hoarded women and treasure, jade and silk; he built palaces, towers, and pavilions without end. Corvée labor knew no season; war never ceased. Outwardly he flaunted might; inwardly he nursed suspicion and malice. Slanderers rose; the loyal were cast aside. Court and people lied to one another until life became unbearable—and so he died by a commoner's hand, a mockery to all the world.

sentences.zh: 聖哲乘機，拯其危溺。

translations.literal: The sage seized the moment and rescued them from peril and drowning.
translations.idiomatic: Then the wise and worthy seized their chance and pulled the realm back from the brink of ruin.

sentences.zh: 今宮觀台榭，盡居之矣；

translations.literal: Now palaces, towers, and pavilions—you occupy them all;
translations.idiomatic: Today, palaces and towers—you already inhabit them all;

sentences.zh: 奇珍異物，盡收之矣；

translations.literal: Rare treasures and strange objects—you have gathered them all;
translations.idiomatic: Rare treasures and exotic wonders—you have gathered them all;

sentences.zh: 姬薑淑媛，盡侍於側矣；

translations.literal: Beautiful consorts and graceful ladies—all attend at your side;
translations.idiomatic: Fair consorts and graceful ladies—all stand in attendance at your side;

sentences.zh: 四海九州，盡為臣妾矣。

translations.literal: The four seas and nine provinces—all have become your servants.
translations.idiomatic: The four seas and nine provinces—all lie at your command.

sentences.zh: 若能鑒彼所以亡，念我所以得，焚寶衣，毀廣殿，安處卑宮，德之上也。

translations.literal: If you can take warning from the cause of their ruin and reflect on the cause of your success—burning precious robes, demolishing vast halls, and dwelling in modest quarters—that is virtue of the highest order.
translations.idiomatic: If you can read in their fall the warning of your own rise—burn the brocade robes, tear down the vast halls, and dwell in humble chambers—that is the highest virtue.

sentences.zh: 若成功不廢，即仍其舊，除其不急，德之次也。

translations.literal: If, having succeeded, you do not abandon the work but keep to the old plan, removing only what is not urgent—that is virtue of the second rank.
translations.idiomatic: If, now that success is won, you do not abandon the work entirely but keep what was begun, stripping away only what is not urgent—that is the next best virtue.

sentences.zh: 不惟王業之艱難，謂天命可恃，因基增舊，甘心侈靡，使人不見德而勞役是聞，斯為下矣。

translations.literal: If you do not reflect on how hard the royal enterprise was won, if you say that Heaven's mandate may be relied upon, if you enlarge the old foundations and willingly indulge in extravagance, so that men hear not of your virtue but only of forced labor—that is the lowest course.
translations.idiomatic: But if you forget how bitterly the throne was won, trust that Heaven's mandate will endure forever, expand the old foundations, and surrender yourself to extravagance—so that the people hear nothing of your virtue, only of their toil—that is the lowest course of all.

sentences.zh: 以暴易暴，與亂同道。

translations.literal: To replace violence with violence is to walk the same road as chaos.
translations.idiomatic: To overthrow tyranny only to become tyrannical yourself is to follow the path of ruin.

sentences.zh: 夫作事不法，後無以觀。

translations.literal: When one's actions do not follow the law, later generations have nothing by which to take measure.
translations.idiomatic: When a ruler's deeds violate the proper way, those who come after have no standard by which to judge him.

sentences.zh: 人怨神怒，則災害生；

translations.literal: When the people resent and the spirits rage, calamities arise;
translations.idiomatic: When the people murmur and the spirits grow angry, disasters follow;

sentences.zh: 災害生，則禍亂作；

translations.literal: When calamities arise, disaster and rebellion follow;
translations.idiomatic: when disasters come, rebellion follows;

sentences.zh: 禍亂作，而能以身名令終鮮矣。

translations.literal: When disaster and rebellion follow, few can preserve their person and name to a good end.
translations.idiomatic: and when rebellion comes, few rulers can preserve their lives and good names to the end.

sentences.zh: 是歲，大雨，穀、洛溢，毀宮寺十九，漂居人六百家。

translations.literal: That year, heavy rains fell; the Gu and Luo rivers overflowed; nineteen palace temples were destroyed, and six hundred households were swept away.
translations.idiomatic: That year came torrential rains. The Gu and Luo rivers burst their banks, destroying nineteen palace temples and sweeping away six hundred households.

sentences.zh: 徵陳事曰：

translations.literal: Wei Zheng set forth the matter, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng laid the matter before the throne, saying:

sentences.zh: 臣聞為國基於德禮，保於誠信。

translations.literal: I have heard that a state is founded upon virtue and ritual, and preserved by sincerity and trust.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that a state is built on virtue and ritual, and sustained by sincerity and trust.

sentences.zh: 誠信立，則下無二情；

translations.literal: When sincerity and trust are established, those below have no divided hearts;
translations.idiomatic: When sincerity and trust stand firm, those below harbor no divided loyalties;

sentences.zh: 德禮形，則遠者來格。

translations.literal: When virtue and ritual take form, those far away come to submit.
translations.idiomatic: when virtue and ritual are made manifest, even distant peoples come to pay homage.

sentences.zh: 故德禮誠信，國之大綱，不可斯須廢也。

translations.literal: Thus virtue, ritual, sincerity, and trust are the great cords of the state and must not be abandoned even for a moment.
translations.idiomatic: Virtue, ritual, sincerity, and trust are the great cords of the state—they must not be set aside even for a moment.

sentences.zh: 傳曰：「君使臣以禮，臣事君以忠。

translations.literal: The Classic says: 'The ruler employs his ministers with ritual; the minister serves his ruler with loyalty.'
translations.idiomatic: The Classic says, 'Let the ruler treat his ministers with ritual; let ministers serve their ruler with loyalty.'

sentences.zh: 」「自古皆有死，民無信不立。

translations.literal: 'From antiquity all men have faced death; a people without trust cannot stand.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Since ancient times, all men must die—but a people without trust cannot endure.'

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「同言而信，信在言前；

translations.literal: It also says: 'When words are alike, trust lies before the words;
translations.idiomatic: It also says, 'When two men speak alike, trust is already present before the words are spoken;

sentences.zh: 同令而行，誠在令外。

translations.literal: When orders are alike, sincerity lies beyond the orders.'
translations.idiomatic: when two commands are alike, sincerity already exists beyond the command itself.'

sentences.zh: 」然則言而不行，言不信也；

translations.literal: Thus, to speak and not act is speech without trust;
translations.idiomatic: Thus, to speak and not act is to speak without trust;

sentences.zh: 令而不從，令無誠也。

translations.literal: To issue orders and not be obeyed is command without sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: to command and not be obeyed is to rule without sincerity.

sentences.zh: 不信之言，不誠之令，君子弗為也。

translations.literal: Words without trust, commands without sincerity—the noble man does not commit them.
translations.idiomatic: Words without trust, commands without sincerity—the noble man will not stoop to such things.

sentences.zh: 自王道休明，綿十餘載，倉廩愈積，土地益廣，然而道德不日博，仁義不日厚，何哉？

translations.literal: Since Your Majesty's enlightened rule began, more than ten years have passed; the granaries grow ever fuller, the land ever broader—yet virtue and morality do not daily expand, benevolence and righteousness do not daily deepen. Why is this?
translations.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty's enlightened reign began, more than ten years have passed. The granaries grow fuller; the realm grows wider—yet virtue does not deepen day by day, nor benevolence and righteousness grow day by day. Why?

sentences.zh: 由待下之情，未盡誠信，雖有善始之勤，而無克終之美。

translations.literal: It is because in treating those below, sincerity and trust have not been fully applied; though there has been diligence at the beginning, there is not the beauty of carrying through to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Because in your dealings with those below, sincerity and trust have not been complete. You have begun well, but not finished well.

sentences.zh: 故便佞之徒得肆其巧，謂同心為朋黨，告訐為至公，強直為擅權，忠讜為誹謗。

translations.literal: Therefore flatterers and sycophants have been able to deploy their cunning, calling unity of purpose factionalism, denunciation the height of public-mindedness, forthrightness usurpation of power, and loyal remonstrance slander.
translations.idiomatic: And so the smooth-tongued and the cunning have had their way: they call unity of purpose 'faction'; they call denunciation 'impartial justice'; they call forthrightness 'grasping for power'; they call loyal remonstrance 'slander.'

sentences.zh: 謂之朋黨，雖忠信可疑；

translations.literal: Call it faction, and even loyalty and trust become suspect;
translations.idiomatic: Call it faction, and even the loyal and trustworthy fall under suspicion;

sentences.zh: 謂之至公，雖矯偽無咎。

translations.literal: Call it the height of public-mindedness, and even pretense and falsehood go unpunished.
translations.idiomatic: call it impartial justice, and even deceit and fraud escape blame.

sentences.zh: 強直者畏擅權而不得盡，忠讜者慮誹謗而不敢與之爭。

translations.literal: The forthright fear being called power-graspers and cannot speak fully; the loyal and outspoken fear being called slanderers and dare not contend.
translations.idiomatic: The forthright fear the charge of grasping for power and cannot speak their full mind; the loyal and outspoken fear the charge of slander and dare not argue back.

sentences.zh: 熒惑視聽，郁于大道，妨化損德，無斯甚者。

translations.literal: To dazzle and confuse what the ruler sees and hears, to obstruct the great Way—nothing harms transformation and diminishes virtue more than this.
translations.idiomatic: To dazzle the ruler's eyes and ears, to block the great Way—nothing does more harm to good governance and virtue.

sentences.zh: 今將致治則委之君子，得失或訪諸小人，是譽毀常在小人，而督責常加君子也。

translations.literal: Now, when you wish to bring about good order you entrust it to noble men, yet when gain or loss is at stake you consult petty men—so praise and blame always rest with petty men, while scrutiny and blame always fall upon noble men.
translations.idiomatic: Today, when you seek good order you rely on noble men—but when something goes wrong, you turn to petty men for advice. Praise and blame thus fall to petty men, while responsibility and censure fall to noble men.

sentences.zh: 夫中智之人，豈無小惠，然慮不及遠，雖使竭力盡誠，猶未免傾敗，況內懷奸利，承顏順旨乎？

translations.literal: Men of middling intelligence—are they without small talents? Yet their thought does not reach far; even if you make them exert all their strength and sincerity, they still cannot avoid ruin. How much less those who harbor wicked profit within and fawn upon your countenance to follow your wishes?
translations.idiomatic: Men of middling wit may have their small talents—but their vision does not reach far. Even if you make them serve with all their strength and sincerity, they cannot save you from disaster. How much less those who harbor secret greed and fawn upon your face to follow your every whim?

sentences.zh: 故孔子曰：「君子而不仁者有矣，未有小人而仁者。

translations.literal: Therefore Confucius said: 'There have been noble men who were not benevolent, but there have never been petty men who were benevolent.'
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, 'There have been noble men who lacked benevolence—but there has never been a petty man who possessed it.'

sentences.zh: 」然則君子不能無小惡，惡不積無害於正；

translations.literal: Thus then, a gentleman cannot be without small faults; if faults do not accumulate, they do not harm uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: Even the noble cannot be wholly free of small failings—but failings that never gather into habit do not corrupt what is upright in them.

sentences.zh: 小人時有小善，善不積不足以忠。

translations.literal: The petty man at times has small virtues; if virtues do not accumulate, it is not enough to constitute loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Even the base man may now and then do a small good—but scattered kindnesses do not add up to true loyalty.

sentences.zh: 今謂之善人矣，復慮其不信，何異立直木而疑其景之曲乎？

translations.literal: Now you call someone a good person, yet still worry that he is untrustworthy—how is this different from setting up a straight tree and suspecting its shadow is crooked?
translations.idiomatic: If you already call a man good, yet still doubt his faithfulness, what is that but planting a straight post and then accusing its shadow of bending?

sentences.zh: 故上不信則無以使下，下不信則無以事上。

translations.literal: Therefore, if the superior does not trust, there is no way to employ subordinates; if subordinates do not trust, there is no way to serve the superior.
translations.idiomatic: When those above withhold trust, they lose the means to command; when those below withhold trust, they lose the means to serve.

sentences.zh: 信之為義大矣！

translations.literal: The meaning of trust is vast indeed!
translations.idiomatic: In governance, nothing weighs more than trust.

sentences.zh: 昔齊桓公問管仲曰：「吾欲使酒腐於爵，肉腐於俎，得無害霸乎？

translations.literal: In former times Duke Huan of Qi asked Guan Zhong: 'I wish to let wine spoil in the cup and meat rot on the chopping block—would this harm my hegemony?'
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Duke Huan of Qi asked Guan Zhong, 'Suppose I let wine go sour in the goblet and meat rot on the board—would that ruin my path to hegemony?'

sentences.zh: 」管仲曰：「此固非其善者，然無害霸也。

translations.literal: Guan Zhong said: 'This is certainly not the best conduct, yet it would not harm hegemony.'
translations.idiomatic: Guan Zhong answered, 'That is hardly the conduct of a great ruler—but it would not, by itself, destroy your hegemony.'

sentences.zh: 」公曰：「何如而害霸？

translations.literal: The Duke said: 'What then would harm hegemony?'
translations.idiomatic: The duke pressed him, 'Then what would destroy it?'

sentences.zh: 」曰：「不能知人，害霸也；

translations.literal: He said: 'Being unable to know men—this harms hegemony;
translations.idiomatic: Guan Zhong said, 'Failing to discern men—that destroys hegemony;

sentences.zh: 知而不能用，害霸也；

translations.literal: knowing but being unable to employ them—this harms hegemony;
