translations.idiomatic: discerning them but failing to use them—that destroys hegemony;

sentences.zh: 用而不能任，害霸也；

translations.literal: employing but being unable to entrust them—this harms hegemony;
translations.idiomatic: using them but failing to empower them—that destroys hegemony;

sentences.zh: 任而不能信，害霸也；

translations.literal: entrusting but being unable to trust them—this harms hegemony;
translations.idiomatic: empowering them but failing to trust them—that destroys hegemony;

sentences.zh: 既信而又使小人參之，害霸也。

translations.literal: having trusted but then letting petty men interfere—this harms hegemony.'
translations.idiomatic: and once you have trusted them, letting petty men meddle in their affairs—that destroys hegemony.'

sentences.zh: 」晉中行穆伯攻鼓，經年而不能下，饋閑倫曰：「鼓之嗇夫，閑倫知之，請無疲士大夫，而鼓可得。

translations.literal: Xun Mubo of Jin attacked the city of Gu; a year passed and he could not capture it. Xian Lun was presented, who said: 'The overseer at Gu—Xian Lun knows him; please do not weary the officers and gentlemen, and Gu may be taken.'
translations.idiomatic: When Xun Mubo of Jin besieged Gu and could not take it for a full year, a man named Xian Lun was brought forward. He said, 'I know the quartermaster at Gu. Do not exhaust your officers and soldiers—let me handle this, and Gu will fall.'

sentences.zh: 」穆伯不應。

translations.literal: Mubo did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Mubo said nothing.

sentences.zh: 左右曰：「不折一戟，不傷一卒，而鼓可得，君奚不為？

translations.literal: Those at his side said: 'Without breaking a single halberd, without wounding a single soldier, and Gu can be taken—why does my lord not do this?'
translations.idiomatic: His attendants urged him, 'Not one halberd broken, not one soldier wounded—and Gu is ours. Why will you not do it?'

sentences.zh: 」穆伯曰：「閑倫之為人也，佞而不仁。

translations.literal: Mubo said: 'As for Xian Lun as a person—he is flattering and unkind.'
translations.idiomatic: Mubo replied, 'Xian Lun is a man of sycophancy, not of humaneness.'

sentences.zh: 若使閑倫下之，吾不可以不賞，若賞之，是賞佞人也。

translations.literal: If I had Xian Lun capture it, I could not fail to reward him; if I rewarded him, I would be rewarding a flatterer.
translations.idiomatic: If I let Xian Lun take the city, I would have no choice but to reward him—and to reward him would be to reward a sycophant.

sentences.zh: 佞人得志，是使晉國舍仁而為佞，雖得鼓，安用之！

translations.literal: If flatterers get their way, this is to make the state of Jin abandon benevolence for flattery—even if we gain Gu, what use is it!'
translations.idiomatic: When sycophants prosper, Jin trades humaneness for flattery. Even if we win Gu, what would it be worth?'

sentences.zh: 」夫穆伯，列國大夫，管仲，霸者之佐，猶能慎于信任，遠避佞人，況陛下之上聖乎？

translations.literal: Mubo was but a minister among the feudal states; Guan Zhong was the aide of a hegemon—yet both were still careful about trust and kept flatterers at a distance; how much more so for Your Majesty, supreme in sagehood?
translations.idiomatic: Mubo was only a minister among rival states; Guan Zhong merely the counselor of a hegemon—yet both still guarded trust with care and kept sycophants at arm's length. How much more should Your Majesty, who stands above all sages?

sentences.zh: 若欲令君子小人是非不雜，必懷之以德，待之以信，厲之以義，節之以禮，然後善善而惡惡，審罰而明賞，無為之化何遠之有！

translations.literal: If you wish to keep the distinction between gentleman and petty man from becoming confused, you must embrace them with virtue, treat them with trust, stimulate them with righteousness, and restrain them with ritual—then cherishing the good and hating the wicked, discerning punishments and clarifying rewards, how far could effortless transformation be!
translations.idiomatic: If you would keep the noble and the base from mingling in confusion, you must hold them with virtue, meet them with trust, sharpen them with righteousness, and bound them with ritual. Then, loving what is good and hating what is evil, weighing punishments and making rewards clear—what distance could there be to rule by effortless transformation?

sentences.zh: 善善而不能進，惡惡而不能去，罰不及有罪，賞不加有功，則危亡之期或未可保。

translations.literal: Cherishing the good yet unable to advance them, hating the wicked yet unable to remove them, punishments not reaching the guilty, rewards not adding to those with merit—then the day of peril and ruin may yet be uncertain in coming.
translations.idiomatic: If you honor the good but cannot promote them, despise the wicked but cannot remove them, punish without reaching the guilty, and reward without reaching the meritorious—then the hour of peril and ruin may not long be delayed.

sentences.zh: 帝手詔嘉答。

translations.literal: The Emperor personally wrote an edict in reply, commending him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor answered with his own hand, praising the memorial.

sentences.zh: 於是，廢明德宮玄圃院賜遭水者。

translations.literal: Thereupon, he abolished the Xuanyuan Court of the Bright Virtue Palace and granted it to those who had suffered from flooding.
translations.idiomatic: At once he closed the Xuanyuan Garden of the Bright Virtue Palace and gave it to those who had lost homes in the floods.

sentences.zh: 它日，宴群臣，帝曰：「貞觀以前，從我定天下，間關草昧，玄齡功也。

translations.literal: On another day, while feasting the ministers, the Emperor said: 'Before the Zhenguan reign, those who followed me to settle the realm through hardship in the wild beginnings—the credit belongs to Xuanling.'
translations.idiomatic: On another day, feasting his ministers, the emperor said, 'Before Zhenguan, when I fought through hardship to settle the realm in its raw beginnings, the credit belonged to Fang Xuanling.'

sentences.zh: 貞觀之後，納忠諫，正朕違，為國家長利，徵而已。

translations.literal: After Zhenguan, receiving loyal remonstrances, correcting my faults, working for the lasting benefit of the state—that was Wei Zheng alone.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhenguan, in receiving loyal counsel, correcting my errors, and securing the long welfare of the state—only Wei Zheng.'

sentences.zh: 雖古名臣，亦何以加！

translations.literal: Even among famed ministers of antiquity—how could one add to this!
translations.idiomatic: Even the greatest ministers of old—who could surpass that?'

sentences.zh: 」親解佩刀，以賜二人。

translations.literal: He personally unsheathed his belt-knife and bestowed it upon the two men.
translations.idiomatic: He took the knife from his own belt and gave it to the two of them.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗問群臣：「徵與諸葛亮孰賢？

translations.literal: The Emperor once asked the ministers: 'Between Wei Zheng and Zhuge Liang—which is worthier?'
translations.idiomatic: Once the emperor asked his ministers, 'Between Wei Zheng and Zhuge Liang—who is the greater man?'

sentences.zh: 」岑文本曰：「亮才兼將相，非徵可比。

translations.literal: Cen Wenben said: 'Liang combined in himself the talents of general and minister—Wei Zheng cannot compare.'
translations.idiomatic: Cen Wenben answered, 'Liang united in one person the gifts of general and chancellor. Wei Zheng cannot match that.'

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「徵蹈履仁義，以弼朕躬，欲致之堯、舜，雖亮無以抗。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: 'Wei Zheng treads and fulfills benevolence and righteousness, assisting my person, wishing to bring me to the level of Yao and Shun—even Liang cannot match him.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, 'Wei Zheng walks in benevolence and righteousness, steadies my rule, and would raise me to the level of Yao and Shun. Even Liang cannot stand against that.'

sentences.zh: 時上封者眾，或不切事，帝厭之，欲加譙黜，徵曰：「古者立謗木，欲聞己過。

translations.literal: At the time many submitted sealed memorials, some not addressing real matters; the Emperor grew weary of them and wished to ridicule and dismiss them. Wei Zheng said: 'In antiquity they set up a wood for criticism, desiring to hear their own faults.
translations.idiomatic: At that time many sealed memorials arrived, some of them trivial; the emperor grew tired of them and wanted to mock and dismiss the writers. Wei Zheng said, 'In old times rulers erected a post for criticism because they wished to hear their own faults.

sentences.zh: 封事，其謗木之遺乎！

translations.literal: Sealed memorials—these are the remnant of the wood for criticism!
translations.idiomatic: These sealed reports are the last echo of that post!'

sentences.zh: 陛下思聞得失，當恣其所陳。

translations.literal: Your Majesty wishes to hear gains and losses—you should let them state whatever they will.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty truly wishes to know what succeeds and what fails, you should let them speak as freely as they please.

sentences.zh: 言而是乎，為朝廷之益；

translations.literal: If their words are correct, it is a benefit to the court;
translations.idiomatic: When they are right, the court gains;

sentences.zh: 非乎，無損於政。

translations.literal: if incorrect, no harm to governance.'
translations.idiomatic: when they are wrong, the realm loses nothing.'

sentences.zh: 」帝悅，皆勞遣之。

translations.literal: The Emperor was pleased and rewarded and sent them all off.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased, thanked each writer, and sent them away.

sentences.zh: 十三年，阿史那結社率作亂，雲陽石然，自冬至五月不雨，徵上疏極言曰：

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, Ashina Jieshelv raised rebellion; stones burned in Yunyang; from winter through the fifth month there was no rain; Wei Zheng submitted a memorial speaking forthrightly, saying:
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, Ashina Jieshelv rebelled; stones burst into flame at Yunyang; from winter until the fifth month no rain fell. Wei Zheng submitted a memorial speaking without reserve:

sentences.zh: 臣奉侍帷幄十餘年，陛下許臣以仁義之道，守而不失；

translations.literal: I have served within the curtained palace for more than ten years; Your Majesty promised me the Way of benevolence and righteousness, to keep and not lose it;
translations.idiomatic: I have served at Your Majesty's side for more than ten years. You pledged to me the way of benevolence and righteousness, to hold fast to it and never let it go;

sentences.zh: 儉約樸素，終始弗渝。

translations.literal: frugality and plain simplicity—from beginning to end, not to waver.
translations.idiomatic: and to live in frugality and plainness, unchanged from first to last.

sentences.zh: 德音在耳，不敢忘也。

translations.literal: Your virtuous words remain in my ears—I dare not forget them.
translations.idiomatic: Your gracious words still ring in my ears, and I dare not forget them.

sentences.zh: 頃年以來，浸不克終。

translations.literal: In recent years, little by little you have not been able to finish what you began.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in recent years you have slowly failed to carry your beginning through to the end.

sentences.zh: 謹用條陳，裨萬分一。

translations.literal: I respectfully submit these points item by item, hoping to help in one ten-thousandth part.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully set out these points one by one, hoping they may aid you in the smallest measure.

sentences.zh: 陛下在貞觀初，清淨寡欲，化被荒外。

translations.literal: Your Majesty at the beginning of Zhenguan was pure and quiet, with few desires; your transforming influence reached even beyond the wilderness.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Zhenguan, Your Majesty lived in clarity and restraint, with few desires, and your transforming virtue reached even the farthest wilds.

sentences.zh: 今萬里遣使，市索駿馬，並訪怪珍。

translations.literal: Now you send envoys ten thousand li, buying and seeking swift horses, and also searching for strange treasures.
translations.idiomatic: Now you send envoys ten thousand li to buy fine horses and hunt for curiosities.

sentences.zh: 昔漢文帝卻千里馬，晉武帝焚雉頭裘。

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Wen of Han refused the thousand-li horse; Emperor Wu of Jin burned the pheasant-head fur cloak.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Han once refused a horse that could run a thousand li; Emperor Wu of Jin once burned a pheasant-head fur robe.

sentences.zh: 陛下居常論議，遠希堯、舜，今所為，更欲處漢文、晉武下乎？

translations.literal: Your Majesty in daily discussions looks far to emulate Yao and Shun—are your present actions instead placing you below Han Wen and Jin Wu?
translations.idiomatic: In your daily counsels you set your gaze on Yao and Shun—do your present deeds now place you below Han Wen and Jin Wu?

sentences.zh: 此不克終一漸也。

translations.literal: This is the first sign of not finishing what you began.
translations.idiomatic: This is the first drift away from carrying your beginning to its end.

sentences.zh: 子貢問治人。

translations.literal: Zigong asked about governing people.
translations.idiomatic: Zigong asked Confucius how to govern men.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：「懍乎若朽索之馭六馬。

translations.literal: Confucius said: 'With trepidation—as if driving six horses with a rotting rope.'
translations.idiomatic: Confucius answered, 'With fear and trembling—as though holding six horses with a rotting rein.'

sentences.zh: 」子貢曰：「何畏哉？

translations.literal: Zigong said: 'What is there to fear?'
translations.idiomatic: Zigong said, 'What is there to fear?'

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「不以道導之，則吾仇也，若何不畏！

translations.literal: He replied: 'If you do not guide them by the Way, they become our enemies—how can we not fear!'
translations.idiomatic: Confucius answered, 'If you do not lead them by the Way, they become your enemies—how can you not fear?'

sentences.zh: 」陛下在貞觀初，護民之勞，煦之如子，不輕營為。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan, Your Majesty cared for the people's toil, warmed them as a parent warms a child, and did not lightly undertake projects.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Zhenguan years, Your Majesty guarded the people's labor, cherished them as a father cherishes a son, and did not lightly launch new undertakings.

sentences.zh: 頃既奢肆，思用人力，乃曰：「百姓無事則易驕，勞役則易使。

translations.literal: Recently, having already grown extravagant, you thought to employ human labor and said: 'When the common people have nothing to do they grow arrogant; when put to corvée labor they are easy to command.'
translations.idiomatic: Lately, grown extravagant, you have turned to conscripting labor, saying, 'When the people have no work they grow proud; when worn down by corvée they are easy to manage.'

sentences.zh: 」自古未有百姓逸樂而致傾敗者，何有逆畏其驕而為勞役哉？

translations.literal: From antiquity there has never been a case of the common people enjoying ease and pleasure yet bringing ruin—why reverse course and fear their pride, only to impose corvée upon them?
translations.idiomatic: Never in history has a state fallen because its people lived in ease and plenty—why dread their contentment and instead wear them down with forced labor?

sentences.zh: 此不克終二漸也。

translations.literal: This is the second sign of not finishing what you began.
translations.idiomatic: This is the second drift away from carrying your beginning to its end.

sentences.zh: 陛下在貞觀初，役己以利物，比來縱欲以勞人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan, Your Majesty taxed yourself to benefit things; lately you indulge your desires at the people's expense.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Zhenguan years, you restrained yourself for the people's good; now you indulge your desires and burden others with the cost.

sentences.zh: 雖憂人之言不絕於口，而樂身之事實切諸心。

translations.literal: Though words of concern for others never leave your lips, matters that please your person are what truly grip your heart.
translations.idiomatic: You speak endlessly of caring for others, yet what truly grips your heart are the pleasures that serve you alone.

sentences.zh: 無慮營構，輒曰：「弗為此，不便我身。

translations.literal: Whenever you contemplate construction, you say: 'If I do not do this, it will be inconvenient for me.'
translations.idiomatic: Whenever you plan some new work, you say, 'If I do not build this, it will be inconvenient for me.'

sentences.zh: 」推之人情，誰敢復爭？

translations.literal: Push this on human feeling—who would dare contend again?
translations.idiomatic: Weigh that against ordinary human feeling—who would dare speak against it?

sentences.zh: 此不克終三漸也。

translations.literal: This is the third sign of not finishing what you began.
translations.idiomatic: This is the third drift away from carrying your beginning to its end.

sentences.zh: 在貞觀初，親君子，斥小人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan, you were close to noble men and kept petty men at a distance.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Zhenguan years, you drew near to noble men and kept petty men at arm's length.

sentences.zh: 比來輕褻小人，禮重君子。

translations.literal: Lately you treat petty men lightly and familiarly, while honoring noble men with ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Lately you have grown familiar with petty men while treating noble men with distant ceremony.

sentences.zh: 重君子也，恭而遠之；

translations.literal: Honoring noble men—you revere them yet keep them afar;
translations.idiomatic: You honor noble men, yet revere them from a distance;

sentences.zh: 輕小人也，狎而近之。

translations.literal: treating petty men lightly—you are familiar with them and draw them near.
translations.idiomatic: you treat petty men lightly, drawing them close in easy familiarity.

sentences.zh: 近之莫見其非，遠之莫見其是。

translations.literal: Drawn near, one does not see their faults; kept afar, one does not see their merits.
translations.idiomatic: Those kept near hide their faults from your sight; those kept far hide their virtues from your sight.

sentences.zh: 莫見其是，則不待間而疏；

translations.literal: Not seeing their merits, then without waiting for an opening one grows estranged;
translations.idiomatic: When you cannot see their merits, estrangement follows without need of cause;

sentences.zh: 莫見其非，則有時而昵。

translations.literal: not seeing their faults, then at times one grows intimate.
translations.idiomatic: when you cannot see their faults, intimacy grows by degrees.

sentences.zh: 昵小人，疏君子，而欲致治，非所聞也。

translations.literal: To be intimate with petty men and estranged from noble men, yet wish to bring about good order—this is unheard of.
translations.idiomatic: To favor petty men, alienate noble men, and still expect good order—there is no precedent for it.

sentences.zh: 此不克終四漸也。

translations.literal: This is the fourth sign of not finishing what you began.
translations.idiomatic: This is the fourth drift away from carrying your beginning to its end.

sentences.zh: 在貞觀初，不貴異物，不作無益。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan, you did not prize strange objects and did not do what was unprofitable.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Zhenguan years, you did not covet rare goods or pursue useless extravagance.

sentences.zh: 而今難得之貨雜然並進，玩好之作無時而息。

translations.literal: But now hard-to-obtain goods crowd in together, and trinkets for amusement never cease.
translations.idiomatic: Now rare treasures pour in from every side, and objects of idle pleasure are sought without pause.

sentences.zh: 上奢靡而望下樸素，力役廣而冀農業興，不可得已。

translations.literal: The ruler extravagant yet hoping the ruled will be plain, corvée broad yet hoping agriculture will flourish—this cannot be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: If the ruler lives in luxury while expecting simplicity below, and broadens forced labor while hoping agriculture will thrive—that cannot be achieved.

sentences.zh: 此不克終五漸也。

translations.literal: This is the fifth sign of not finishing what you began.
translations.idiomatic: This is the fifth drift away from carrying your beginning to its end.

sentences.zh: 貞觀之初，求士如渴，賢者所舉，即信而任之，取其所長，常恐不及。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan, you sought worthy men as if thirsty; whomever the worthy recommended, you trusted and employed at once, taking their strong points, always fearing you might fall short.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Zhenguan years, you thirsted for talent; whomever the worthy recommended, you trusted and appointed, taking what they offered and fearing only that you might fall short.

sentences.zh: 比來由心好惡，以眾賢舉而用，以一人毀而棄，雖積年任而信，或一朝疑而斥。

translations.literal: Lately you follow the likes and dislikes of your heart: if many worthy men recommend someone, you employ him; if one person slanders him, you discard him—even if he has served for years in trust, he may in one morning be suspected and driven off.
translations.idiomatic: Lately you follow your own likes and dislikes: when many worthy men recommend someone, you use him; when one man speaks against him, you cast him aside—even a man trusted for years may be rejected in a single morning.

sentences.zh: 夫行有素履，事有成跡，一人之毀未必可信，積年之行不應頓虧。

translations.literal: Conduct has its constant tread; affairs leave their settled tracks. One man's slander is not necessarily to be believed; years of conduct should not suddenly be ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Character has its steady path; service leaves its record. One man's slander is not necessarily true, and years of faithful conduct should not be undone in an instant.

sentences.zh: 陛下不察其原，以為臧否，使讒佞得行，守道疏間。

translations.literal: Your Majesty does not examine the root cause and treats slander as judgment of good and bad, so flatterers and sycophants get their way while those who keep to the Way are driven apart.
translations.idiomatic: Without examining the root of the matter, you take slander for judgment of merit, letting flatterers prevail while men of integrity are pushed aside.

sentences.zh: 此不克終六漸也。

translations.literal: This is the sixth sign of not finishing what you began.
translations.idiomatic: This is the sixth drift away from carrying your beginning to its end.

sentences.zh: 在貞觀初，高居深拱，無田獵畢弋之好。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan, you sat high and deep in repose, with no taste for hunting, falconry, or archery.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Zhenguan years, you held yourself aloof in dignified repose, with no love of hunting, hawking, or the chase.

sentences.zh: 數年之後，志不克固，鷹犬之貢，遠及四夷，晨出夕返，馳騁為樂，變起不測，其及救乎？

translations.literal: Several years later, your will could not hold firm: tribute of hawks and hounds came from the four quarters; you went out at dawn and returned at dusk, galloping for pleasure—if unforeseen trouble arose, could you be saved in time?
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years your resolve weakened: hawks and hounds arrived as tribute from the four directions; you rode out at dawn and returned at dusk for sport—if disaster struck suddenly, could help reach you in time?

sentences.zh: 此不克終七漸也。

translations.literal: This is the seventh sign of not finishing what you began.
translations.idiomatic: This is the seventh drift away from carrying your beginning to its end.

sentences.zh: 在貞觀初，遇下有禮，群情上達。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan, you treated those below with courtesy, and the feelings of the multitude reached upward.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Zhenguan years, you treated subordinates with courtesy, and the people's sentiments could reach you.

sentences.zh: 今外官奏事，顏色不接，間因所短，詰其細過，雖有忠款，而不得申。

translations.literal: Now when officials outside the capital submit memorials, you do not receive them with a welcoming countenance; sometimes, seizing on some small fault, you press them over minor errors—though they have loyal intent, they cannot fully express it.
translations.idiomatic: Now when provincial officials submit memorials, your face shows no welcome; sometimes you seize on a small fault and harry them over trifles—though their loyalty is genuine, they cannot fully speak their mind.

sentences.zh: 此不克終八漸也。

translations.literal: This is the eighth sign of not finishing what you began.
translations.idiomatic: This is the eighth drift away from carrying your beginning to its end.

sentences.zh: 在貞觀初，孜孜治道，常若不足。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan, you toiled unceasingly at governing the Way, as though it were never enough.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Zhenguan years, you labored tirelessly at governance, as if you could never do enough.

sentences.zh: 比恃功業之大，負聖智之明，長慠縱欲，無事興兵，問罪遠裔。

translations.literal: Lately, relying on the greatness of your achievements and the brilliance of your sage wisdom, you have long grown proud and indulged your desires, raising armies without cause and calling distant lands to account.
translations.idiomatic: Lately, trusting in the scale of your achievements and the brilliance of your wisdom, you have grown proud and willful, launching wars without need and punishing distant peoples.

sentences.zh: 親狎者阿旨不肯諫，疏遠者畏威不敢言。

translations.literal: Those close and intimate flatter your wishes and will not remonstrate; those distant and removed fear your authority and dare not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Those near you echo your wishes and will not remonstrate; those far from you fear your power and dare not speak.

sentences.zh: 積而不已，所損非細。

translations.literal: If this accumulates without end, the harm will not be slight.
translations.idiomatic: If this goes on unchecked, the damage will be no small matter.

sentences.zh: 此不克終九漸也。

translations.literal: This is the ninth sign of not finishing what you began.
translations.idiomatic: This is the ninth drift away from carrying your beginning to its end.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，頻年霜旱，畿內戶口並就關外，攜老扶幼，來往數年，卒無一戶亡去。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan, for years there were frost and drought; households within the capital region all moved beyond the passes, carrying the old and leading the young, coming and going for years—yet in the end not a single household fled away.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Zhenguan years, frost and drought struck year after year; families in the capital region moved beyond the passes, old and young together, traveling back and forth for years—yet not one household finally fled.

sentences.zh: 此由陛下矜育撫寧，故死不攜貳也。

translations.literal: This was because Your Majesty cherished, nurtured, and reassured them, so that even in death they did not waver in loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: That was because Your Majesty cherished and reassured them, so that even unto death they did not abandon their loyalty.

sentences.zh: 比者疲於徭役，關中之人，勞弊尤甚。

translations.literal: Lately, worn down by corvée, the people of Guanzhong have suffered exhaustion above all.
translations.idiomatic: Lately, worn down by corvée, the people of the Guanzhong region have suffered most grievously.

sentences.zh: 雜匠當下，顧而不遣。

translations.literal: Miscellaneous artisans due for release are looked at yet not sent away.
translations.idiomatic: Artisans due to be dismissed are overlooked and kept on.

sentences.zh: 正兵番上，復別驅任。

translations.literal: Regular soldiers on rotation for palace duty are again separately conscripted for other tasks.
translations.idiomatic: Regular troops rotating for palace duty are again pressed into separate assignments.

sentences.zh: 市物繈屬於廛，遞子背望於道。

translations.literal: Goods bought in the markets stream from the shops; relay runners and porters crowd the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Purchases from the markets pour in unceasingly; couriers and porters throng the roads.

sentences.zh: 脫有一穀不收，百姓之心，恐不能如前日之帖泰。

translations.literal: If there should be a year when the grain harvest fails, the hearts of the common people—I fear they cannot be as settled and secure as in days past.
translations.idiomatic: Should even one harvest fail, I fear the people's hearts will no longer be as calm and secure as before.

sentences.zh: 此不克終十漸也。

translations.literal: This is the tenth sign of not finishing what you began.
translations.idiomatic: This is the tenth drift away from carrying your beginning to its end.

sentences.zh: 夫禍福無門，惟人之召，人無釁焉，妖不妄作。

translations.literal: Fortune and calamity have no gate of their own—only men summon them; when men give no cause, portents do not arise without reason.
translations.idiomatic: Fortune and disaster have no door of their own—only men open them; when men give no cause, strange omens do not appear at random.

sentences.zh: 今旱熯之災，遠被郡國，凶醜之孽，起於轂下，此上天示戒，乃陛下恐懼憂勤之日也。

translations.literal: Now drought and scorching heat reach distant commanderies and districts; vicious and ugly evils have risen beneath the capital—this is a warning shown by Heaven, and a day when Your Majesty should feel fear, dread, and diligent concern.
translations.idiomatic: Now drought and heat afflict distant regions; foul omens have appeared at the capital itself—this is Heaven's warning, and a day for Your Majesty to feel fear and redouble your care.

sentences.zh: 千載休期，時難再得，明主可為而不為，臣所以鬱結長歎者也！

translations.literal: An age of great peace comes once in a thousand years and is hard to grasp twice; when a clear-sighted ruler can act yet does not, that is why your servant is bound in grief and long sighs!
translations.idiomatic: An age of lasting peace comes once in a thousand years and cannot be seized twice; when a wise ruler can act and does not—that is why I am choked with grief and long sighs!

sentences.zh: 疏奏，帝曰：「朕今聞過矣，願改之，以終善道。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the Emperor said: 'I have now heard my faults and wish to reform, to carry the good Way to its end.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached him, the Emperor said, 'I have heard my faults and mean to amend them, to carry the good path through to the end.

sentences.zh: 有違此言，當何施顏面與公相見哉！

translations.literal: If I go against these words, with what face could I meet you again!'
translations.idiomatic: If I break this promise, how could I face you again?'

sentences.zh: 方以所上疏，列為屏障，庶朝夕見之，兼錄付史官，使萬世知君臣之義。

translations.literal: He ordered the submitted memorial set up as a screen, hoping to see it morning and evening, and also had it copied for the historiographers, so that ten thousand generations might know the righteousness between ruler and minister.
translations.idiomatic: He had the memorial mounted as a screen to read morning and evening, and ordered a copy placed in the historical archives so that future ages would know the bond between ruler and minister.

sentences.zh: 」因賜黃金十斤，馬二匹。

translations.literal: He thereupon bestowed ten catties of gold and two horses.
translations.idiomatic: He then rewarded Wei Zheng with ten catties of gold and two horses.

sentences.zh: 高昌平，帝宴兩儀殿，歎曰：「高昌若不失德，豈至於亡！

translations.literal: When Gaochang was pacified, the Emperor feasted in the Liangyi Hall and sighed: 'If Gaochang had not lost virtue, how could it have come to ruin!
translations.idiomatic: When Gaochang was conquered, the Emperor banqueted in the Liangyi Hall and sighed, 'If Gaochang had not lost its virtue, how could it have perished!

sentences.zh: 然朕亦當自戒，不以小人之言而議君子，庶幾獲安也。

translations.literal: Yet I too must take warning for myself, not to judge noble men by the words of petty men, and perhaps then I may find security.'
translations.idiomatic: Yet I too must take warning, not to judge noble men by petty men's words—then perhaps I may keep my footing.'

sentences.zh: 」徵曰：「昔齊桓公與管仲、鮑叔牙、甯戚四人者飲，桓公請叔牙曰：'盍起為寡人壽？

translations.literal: Wei Zheng said: 'Formerly Duke Huan of Qi drank with four men—Guan Zhong, Bao Shuya, and Ning Qi. Duke Huan asked Shuya: "Will you rise and toast for me?"'
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng said, 'Long ago Duke Huan of Qi drank with Guan Zhong, Bao Shuya, and Ning Qi. The duke asked Shuya, "Will you rise and propose a toast for me?"'

sentences.zh: '叔牙奉觴而起曰：'願公無忘在莒時，使管仲無忘束縛于魯時，使甯戚無忘飯牛車下時。

translations.literal: Shuya took the cup and rose, saying: 'May you, my lord, not forget the time in Ju; may Guan Zhong not forget being bound in Lu; may Ning Qi not forget feeding oxen beneath his cart.'
translations.idiomatic: Shuya took the cup and rose, saying, 'May you, my lord, not forget your days in Ju; may Guan Zhong not forget when he was bound in Lu; may Ning Qi not forget when he fed oxen beneath his cart.'

sentences.zh: '桓公避席而謝曰：'寡人與二大夫能無忘夫子之言，則社稷不危矣。

translations.literal: Duke Huan left his seat and apologized: 'I and the two great officers—if we can not forget the Master's words, then the altars of state will not be in peril.'
translations.idiomatic: Duke Huan left his seat and apologized, 'If I and these two ministers do not forget your words, the altars of state will not be endangered.'

sentences.zh: '」帝曰：「朕不敢忘布衣時，公不得忘叔牙之為人也。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: 'I dare not forget my days in plain cloth; you must not forget how Shuya acted.'
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, 'I shall not forget my days as a commoner; you must not forget how Bao Shuya conducted himself.'

sentences.zh: 帝遣使者至西域立葉護可汗，未還，又遣使齎金帛諸國市馬。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent envoys to the Western Regions to install Ashina Qilibi as qaghan; before they returned, he sent another mission bearing gold and silks to the various states to buy horses.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent envoys to the Western Regions to install Ashina Qilibi as qaghan; before they returned, he sent another mission with gold and silks to the various states to buy horses.

sentences.zh: 徵曰：「今立可汗未定，即詣諸國市馬，彼必以為意在馬，不在立可汗。

translations.literal: Wei Zheng said: 'The qaghan is not yet firmly installed, yet you immediately go to the various states to buy horses—they will surely think your intent lies in the horses, not in installing the qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng said, 'The qaghan is not yet firmly established, yet you already send buyers to the various states—they will surely think your heart is set on horses, not on enthroning the qaghan.

sentences.zh: 可汗得立，必不懷恩。

translations.literal: If the qaghan is installed, he will surely not feel gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: Even if the qaghan is installed, he will not feel bound by gratitude.

sentences.zh: 諸蕃聞之，以中國薄義重利，未必得馬而先失義矣。

translations.literal: When the various tribes hear of it, they will think the Middle Kingdom values profit lightly and esteems righteousness lightly—you may not get the horses and will first lose righteousness.'
translations.idiomatic: When the frontier peoples hear of it, they will think China prizes profit over faith—you may fail to gain the horses and will lose righteousness first.'

sentences.zh: 魏文帝欲求市西域大珠，蘇則以為惠及四海，則不求自至；

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Wei once wished to buy a great pearl from the Western Regions; Su Ze said that when grace extends to the four seas, things sought need not be sought—they come of themselves;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Wei once wished to buy a great pearl from the Western Regions; Su Ze said that when grace reaches the four seas, what is sought arrives unbidden;

sentences.zh: 求而得之，不足貴也。

translations.literal: what is obtained by seeking is not worth cherishing.
translations.idiomatic: what must be chased down is not worth cherishing.

sentences.zh: 陛下可不畏蘇則言乎！

translations.literal: Your Majesty—can you not hold Su Ze's words in awe!'
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty—should you not heed Su Ze's warning?'

sentences.zh: 」帝遂止。

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor thereupon abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 是後右僕射缺，欲用徵，徵讓，得不拜。

translations.literal: After this the post of Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs was vacant; the Emperor wished to appoint Wei Zheng, but Wei Zheng declined and was not invested.
translations.idiomatic: Later the post of Right Vice Director fell vacant; the Emperor wished to appoint Wei Zheng, but Wei Zheng declined and the appointment was not made.

sentences.zh: 皇太子承乾與魏王泰交惡，帝曰：「當今忠謇貴重無逾徵，我遣傅皇太子，一天下之望，羽翼固矣。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Chengan and Prince Wei of Li had grown hostile to each other. The Emperor said: 'Today no one is more valued for loyalty and bluntness than Wei Zheng; I send him to tutor the Crown Prince—once the hope of the empire is fixed, his wings will be strong.'
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Chengan and Prince Li of Wei had fallen out. The Emperor said, 'Today no one surpasses Wei Zheng in loyal bluntness; I appoint him tutor to the Crown Prince—when the empire's hopes rest on him, his support will be secure.'

sentences.zh: 」即拜太子太師。

translations.literal: He thereupon appointed him Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon appointed Wei Zheng Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 徵以疾辭，詔答曰：「漢太子以四皓為助，我賴公，其義也。

translations.literal: Wei Zheng pleaded illness; an edict answered: 'The Han crown prince had the Four Ho as his help; I rely on you—that is the meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng pleaded illness; the Emperor replied, 'The Han crown prince had the Four Ho to assist him; I rely on you in the same way.

sentences.zh: 公雖臥，可擁全之。

translations.literal: Though you lie abed, you can still embrace and preserve him.'
translations.idiomatic: Even lying ill, you can still guard and sustain him.'

sentences.zh: 十七年，疾甚。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, his illness grew severe.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Zhenguan, his illness grew grave.

sentences.zh: 徵家初無正寢，帝命輟小殿材為營構，五日畢，並賜素褥布被，以從其尚。

translations.literal: Wei Zheng's house at first had no main chamber; the Emperor ordered small-hall timber withheld to build one for him, finished in five days, and also bestowed plain bedding and cloth quilts, following his frugal tastes.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng's home at first had no proper main hall; the Emperor ordered timber from a small palace withheld to build one for him, finished in five days, and sent plain bedding and cotton quilts suited to his austere habits.

sentences.zh: 令中郎將宿其第，動靜輒以聞，藥膳賜遺無算，中使者綴道。

translations.literal: He ordered a palace attendant to lodge at his residence; his every movement was reported, and medicines and food sent as gifts were beyond counting, palace envoys crowding the road.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered a palace attendant to stay at Wei Zheng's house; every change in his condition was reported, and gifts of medicine and food were beyond count, palace messengers filling the road.

sentences.zh: 帝親問疾，屏左右，語終日乃還。

translations.literal: The Emperor personally inquired after his illness, dismissed those attending, and spoke with him the whole day before returning.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor came in person to ask after him, dismissed attendants, and talked with him all day before returning.

sentences.zh: 後復與太子臻至徵第，徵加朝服，拖帶。

translations.literal: Later he again went with the Crown Prince to Wei Zheng's house; Wei Zheng put on court robes, dragging his sash.
translations.idiomatic: Later he visited again with the Crown Prince; Wei Zheng donned court robes, the sash trailing from weakness.

sentences.zh: 帝悲懣，拊之流涕，問所欲。

translations.literal: The Emperor was grieved and aggrieved, stroked him and wept, and asked what he wished.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor grieved, stroked him and wept, and asked what he desired.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「嫠不恤緯，而憂宗周之亡！

translations.literal: He replied: 'A widow does not grieve over insufficient weaving, but fears the fall of the Zhou house!'
translations.idiomatic: He answered, 'A widow does not fret over thin cloth, but fears the fall of the royal house!'

sentences.zh: 」帝將以衡山公主降其子叔玉。

translations.literal: The Emperor intended to marry the Princess of Hengshan to his son Shuyu.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor planned to marry the Princess of Hengshan to Wei Zheng's son Shuyu.

sentences.zh: 時主亦從，帝曰：「公強視新婦！

translations.literal: The princess was also present; the Emperor said: 'Sir, look well upon your new bride!'
translations.idiomatic: The princess was present; the Emperor said, 'Look upon your new daughter-in-law while you can!'

sentences.zh: 」徵不能謝。

translations.literal: Wei Zheng could not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng could not answer.

sentences.zh: 是夕，帝夢徵若平生，及旦，薨。

translations.literal: That night the Emperor dreamed of Wei Zheng as in life; at dawn, Wei Zheng died.
translations.idiomatic: That night the Emperor dreamed of Wei Zheng as in life; at dawn Wei Zheng died.

sentences.zh: 帝臨哭，為之慟，罷朝五日。

translations.literal: The Emperor came in person to mourn, grieved for him, and suspended court for five days.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor came in person to mourn, grieved deeply, and suspended court for five days.

sentences.zh: 太子舉哀西華堂。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince observed mourning in the Xihua Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince led mourning rites in the Xihua Hall.

sentences.zh: 詔內外百官朝集使皆赴喪，贈司空、相州都督，諡曰文貞，給羽葆、鼓吹、班劍四十人，陪葬昭陵。

translations.literal: An edict ordered all civil and military officials and tribute envoys from within and without to attend the funeral; he was posthumously made Minister of Works and Area Commander of Xiangzhou, given the posthumous title Wenzhen, granted feathered parasols, musical escort, and a guard of forty halberds, and buried near Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: An edict summoned all officials and envoys to the funeral; he was posthumously made Minister of Works and Area Commander of Xiangzhou, titled Wenzhen, granted feathered parasols, musical escort, and forty halberds of honor, and buried near Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 將葬，其妻裴辭曰：「徵素儉約，今假一品禮，儀物褒大，非徵志。

translations.literal: When the burial was about to take place, his wife Pei declined: 'Wei Zheng was always frugal; now borrowing first-rank rites—the ceremonial objects are too grand; this is not Wei Zheng's wish.'
translations.idiomatic: As burial approached, his wife Lady Pei objected, 'Wei Zheng lived always in frugality; to borrow first-rank funeral rites with such grand display is not what he would have wanted.'

sentences.zh: 」見許，乃用素車，白布幨帷，無塗車、芻靈。

translations.literal: When this was granted, they used a plain carriage with white cloth curtains on the canopy, without lacquered carriage or straw effigy.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor agreed, they used a plain cart with white cloth curtains, without lacquered carriage or straw effigy.

sentences.zh: 帝登苑西樓，望哭盡哀。

translations.literal: The Emperor ascended the western tower of the imperial park and looked toward the funeral, weeping with full grief.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor climbed the western tower of the imperial park, looked toward the funeral procession, and wept his fill.

sentences.zh: 晉王奉詔致祭。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin, by imperial order, performed the sacrificial rites.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin, by imperial command, performed the sacrificial offerings.

sentences.zh: 帝作文於碑，遂書之。

translations.literal: The Emperor composed the text for the stele and himself wrote it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor composed the inscription for the stele and wrote it in his own hand.

sentences.zh: 又賜家封戶九百。

translations.literal: He also bestowed nine hundred fief households on the family.
translations.idiomatic: He also granted the family nine hundred fief households.

sentences.zh: 帝后臨朝歎曰：「以銅為鑒，可正衣冠；

translations.literal: Later, holding court, the Emperor sighed: 'Take bronze as a mirror and you can straighten your robes and cap;
translations.idiomatic: Later at court the Emperor sighed, 'Take bronze for a mirror and you can set your cap and robes aright;

sentences.zh: 以古為鑒，可知興替；

translations.literal: take antiquity as a mirror and you can know rise and fall;
translations.idiomatic: take history for a mirror and you can see the rise and fall of ages;

sentences.zh: 以人為鑒，可明得失。

translations.literal: take other men as a mirror and you can discern gain and loss.
translations.idiomatic: take other men for a mirror and you can know success and failure.

sentences.zh: 朕嘗保此三鑒，內防己過。

translations.literal: I once kept these three mirrors to guard against my own faults within.'
translations.idiomatic: I once kept these three mirrors to guard against my own faults.'

sentences.zh: 今魏徵逝，一鑒亡矣。

translations.literal: Now Wei Zheng has passed away—one mirror is lost.
translations.idiomatic: Now that Wei Zheng is gone, one of those mirrors is lost.

sentences.zh: 朕比使人至其家，得書一紙，始半稿，其可識者曰：'天下之事，有善有惡，任善人則國安，用惡人則國弊。

translations.literal: I recently sent someone to his house and obtained a sheet of writing, only half finished in draft; the legible part says: 'Affairs under Heaven have good and evil; employ good men and the state is secure, employ evil men and the state is ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Recently I sent an envoy to his home and found a single sheet of writing, still only half drafted; the legible portion reads, 'All affairs under Heaven have their good and their evil—put good men in charge and the realm is secure; put wicked men in power and the realm is ruined.

sentences.zh: 公卿之內，情有愛憎，憎者惟見其惡，愛者止見其善。

translations.literal: Among dukes and ministers, feelings have love and hatred; those who hate see only their evil, those who love see only their good.
translations.idiomatic: Among the high ministers, affection and dislike run deep; those who dislike a man see only his faults, those who favor him see only his virtues.

sentences.zh: 愛憎之間，所宜詳慎。

translations.literal: Between love and hatred, one ought to be careful in detail.
translations.idiomatic: In the sway of personal feeling, one must weigh matters with extra care.

sentences.zh: 若愛而知其惡，憎而知其善，去邪勿疑，任賢勿猜，可以興矣。

translations.literal: If in loving one also knows their evil, in hating one also knows their good, remove the wicked without hesitation, employ the worthy without suspicion—then one can flourish.
translations.idiomatic: If you can love a man yet see his faults, or dislike him yet see his merits—cast out the corrupt without wavering, trust the worthy without suspicion—the state may thrive again.

sentences.zh: '其大略如此。

translations.literal: 'Its general purport was thus.
translations.idiomatic: 'That was the gist of it.

sentences.zh: 朕顧思之，恐不免斯過。

translations.literal: I consider it and fear I cannot avoid this fault.
translations.idiomatic: When I reflect on it, I fear I cannot escape this very failing.

sentences.zh: 公卿侍臣可書之於笏，知而必諫也。

translations.literal: Dukes, ministers, and attendant officials may write it on their ceremonial tablets—once aware, they must remonstrate.
translations.idiomatic: Let every minister and attendant official write these words on his court tablet—knowing of a fault, remonstrate without fail.

sentences.zh: 徵狀貌不逾中人，有志膽，每犯顏進諫，雖逢帝甚怒，神色不徙，而天子亦為霽威。

translations.literal: Wei Zheng's appearance did not exceed that of an ordinary man, yet he had resolve and courage; each time he braved the Emperor's displeasure to remonstrate, even when the Emperor was greatly angered his expression did not shift, and the Son of Heaven too would soften his wrath.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng looked no more striking than any ordinary man, yet he had nerve and daring; he would speak against the Emperor's will again and again, and even when the Emperor flew into a rage his face never changed—until the Son of Heaven himself relented.

sentences.zh: 議者謂賁、育不能過。

translations.literal: Commentators said even Meng Ben and Xia Yu could not surpass him.
translations.idiomatic: Observers said that not even the legendary braves Meng Ben and Xia Yu could match him.

sentences.zh: 嘗上塚還，奏曰：「向聞陛下有關南之行，既辦而止，何也？

translations.literal: Once, returning from visiting his tomb, he memorialized: 'I recently heard that Your Majesty had a journey to Guannan, which was prepared and then halted—why?
translations.idiomatic: Once, on returning from tending his father's grave, he submitted a memorial: 'I heard lately that Your Majesty planned a tour to Guannan, made ready, then stopped—why?

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「畏卿，遂停耳。

translations.literal: ' The Emperor said: 'I feared you, and so I stopped.
translations.idiomatic: ' The Emperor said, 'I was afraid of your remonstrance, so I called it off.

sentences.zh: 」始，喪亂後，典章湮散，徵奏引諸儒校集秘書，國家圖籍粲然完整。

translations.literal: ' At the beginning, after the chaos of rebellion, statutes and regulations were scattered and lost; Wei Zheng memorialized to summon various Confucian scholars to collate and gather the secretariat books, and the state's archives became brilliantly complete.
translations.idiomatic: ' In the aftermath of the rebellions, law and ritual had fallen into disarray; Wei Zheng petitioned to gather Confucian scholars to collate the palace library, until the empire's records stood complete and in order.

sentences.zh: 嘗以《小戴禮》綜匯不倫，更作《類禮》二十篇，數年而成。

translations.literal: He once took the Lesser Dai Rites, whose compilation was disorderly, and reworked it into the Categorized Rites in twenty chapters, completed over several years.
translations.idiomatic: Finding the Lesser Dai Rites poorly arranged, he reorganized them into the Categorized Rites in twenty chapters, a work of several years.

sentences.zh: 帝美其書，錄寘內府。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised the book and had it copied and placed in the inner treasury.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor praised the work and had it copied into the inner archive.

sentences.zh: 帝本以兵定天下，雖已治，不忘經略四夷也。

translations.literal: The Emperor had originally settled the realm by arms; though already governed, he did not forget strategizing against the four barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had won the realm by the sword; though the land was at peace, he never ceased planning campaigns on the frontiers.

sentences.zh: 故徵侍宴，奏《破陣武德舞》，則俯首不顧，至《慶善樂》，則諦玩無斁，舉有所諷切如此。

translations.literal: Thus when Wei Zheng attended banquets, if the Breaking Formation Martial Virtue Dance was performed he would bow his head and not look; when the Celebrating Goodness Music came, he would listen with absorbed delight without satiety—his actions carried pointed admonition such as this.
translations.idiomatic: At court feasts, when the Breaking Formation Martial Virtue Dance was performed Wei Zheng would bow his head and refuse to watch; when the Celebrating Goodness Music played, he would listen with rapt pleasure—each gesture a quiet rebuke.

sentences.zh: 徵亡，帝思不已，登淩煙閣觀畫像，賦詩悼痛，聞者媢之，毀短百為。

translations.literal: When Wei Zheng died, the Emperor's thoughts would not cease; he ascended Lingyan Pavilion to view the portrait, composed a poem of mourning grief; those who heard envied him, and slanderers heaped calumny in every way.
translations.idiomatic: After Wei Zheng's death the Emperor could not stop thinking of him; he climbed Lingyan Pavilion to gaze at his portrait and wrote verses of mourning. Envious courtiers seized the moment to slander him without restraint.

sentences.zh: 徵嘗薦杜正倫、侯君集才任宰相，及正倫以罪黜，君集坐逆誅，纖人遂指為阿黨；

translations.literal: Wei Zheng had once recommended Du Zhenglun and Hou Junji as talents fit to be chancellor; when Zhenglun was dismissed for crime and Junji was executed for treason, petty men then pointed to this as factional favoritism;
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng had once recommended Du Zhenglun and Hou Junji as men fit for the chancellorship; when Zhenglun was disgraced and Junji executed for rebellion, small-minded men denounced him as a patron of cliques;

sentences.zh: 又言徵嘗錄前後諫爭語示史官褚遂良。

translations.literal: they also said Wei Zheng had recorded his remonstrances before and after and shown them to the historiographer Chu Suiliang.
translations.idiomatic: they also claimed he had copied his past remonstrances and shown them to the historiographer Chu Suiliang.

sentences.zh: 帝滋不悅，乃停叔玉昏，而仆所為碑，顧其家衰矣。

translations.literal: The Emperor grew ever more displeased, stopped Shuyu's marriage, and toppled the stele he had made; only then did he look upon the family's decline.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's displeasure deepened; he halted Shuyu's marriage, cast down the stele he himself had erected, and let the family fall from favor.

sentences.zh: 遼東之役，高麗、靺鞨犯陣，李勣等力戰破之。

translations.literal: In the Liaodong campaign, Goguryeo and Mohe broke the battle line; Li Ji and others fought fiercely and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: During the Liaodong campaign, Goguryeo and Mohe forces breached the line; Li Ji and others fought hard and broke them.

sentences.zh: 軍還，悵然曰：「魏徵若在，吾有此行邪！

translations.literal: When the army returned, he said despondently: 'If Wei Zheng were still alive, would I have made this expedition!
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return he said wistfully, 'If Wei Zheng were still alive, would I have launched this campaign at all!

sentences.zh: 」即召其家到行在，賜勞妻子，以少牢祠其墓，復立碑，恩禮加焉。

translations.literal: ' He immediately summoned the family to the imperial camp, bestowed rewards on wife and children, sacrificed with the lesser tai offering at his tomb, re-erected the stele, and added to the favors and rites.
translations.idiomatic: ' He at once summoned the family to his camp, rewarded wife and children, offered the lesser tai sacrifice at the tomb, raised the stele again, and restored their honors.

sentences.zh: 四子：叔玉、叔琬、叔璘、叔瑜。

translations.literal: Four sons: Shuyu, Shuwan, Shulin, and Shuyu.
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons: Shuyu, Shuwan, Shulin, and Shuyu.

sentences.zh: 叔玉襲爵為光祿少卿。

translations.literal: Shuyu inherited the title and served as Vice Director of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: Shuyu inherited the marquisate and served as Vice Director of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，以其子膺紹封。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Shenlong era, his son Ying received renewed enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: In the opening years of the Shenlong reign, his son Ying was re-enfeoffed.

sentences.zh: 叔璘，禮部侍郎，武后時，為酷吏所殺。

translations.literal: Shulin, Vice Minister of Rites—in Empress Wu's time was killed by cruel officials.
translations.idiomatic: Shulin, Vice Minister of Rites, was put to death by the empress's brutal magistrates during Wu Zetian's reign.

sentences.zh: 叔瑜，豫州刺史，善草隸，以筆意傅其子華及甥薛稷。

translations.literal: Shuyu, Prefect of Yuzhou, skilled in cursive and clerical script, transmitted his brush intent to his son Hua and his nephew by marriage Xue Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Shuyu, Prefect of Yuzhou, excelled in cursive and clerical script and passed his brushwork to his son Hua and his nephew-in-law Xue Ji.

sentences.zh: 世稱善書者「前有虞、褚，後有薛、魏」。

translations.literal: The age praised masters of calligraphy: 'Before there were Yu and Chu; after there are Xue and Wei.'
translations.idiomatic: Calligraphy masters were said to run 'from Yu and Chu in the earlier age to Xue and Wei in the later.'

sentences.zh: 華為檢校太子左庶子、武陽縣男。

translations.literal: Hua served as Supervising Secretary to the Heir Apparent's Left Wing and was enfeoffed as Baron of Wuyang.
translations.idiomatic: Hua served as Supervising Secretary to the Left Wing of the Heir Apparent and held the title Baron of Wuyang.

sentences.zh: 開元中，寢堂火，子孫哭三日，詔百官赴吊。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era, fire consumed the sleeping hall; descendants mourned three days, and an edict summoned all officials to attend the funeral rites.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kaiyuan, fire destroyed the family hall; his descendants mourned three days while an edict called every official to the funeral.

sentences.zh: 徵五世孫謨。

translations.literal: Wei Zheng's fifth-generation descendant Mo.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng's fifth-generation descendant was Mo.

sentences.zh: 五世孫 謨謨，字申之，擢進士第，同州刺史楊汝士辟為長春宮巡官。

translations.literal: Fifth-generation descendant Mo, style name Shenzhi, passed the jinshi examination; Yang Rushi, Prefect of Tongzhou, recruited him as patrol officer of the Changchun Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Mo, of the fifth generation, styled Shenzhi, passed the jinshi examination and was engaged by Yang Rushi, Prefect of Tongzhou, as patrol officer of the Changchun Palace.

sentences.zh: 文宗讀《貞觀政要》，思徵賢，詔訪其後，汝士薦為右拾遺。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong read the Zhenguan Administration Essentials, recalled Wei Zheng's worth, and ordered a search for his descendants; Rushi recommended him as Right Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: Reading the Zhenguan Administration Essentials, Emperor Wenzong sought Wei Zheng's line; Rushi recommended Mo as Right Reminder.

sentences.zh: 謨姿宇魁秀，帝異之。

translations.literal: Mo's bearing was tall and striking; the Emperor marked him as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Mo was tall and commanding in bearing; the Emperor took him for a man out of the ordinary.

sentences.zh: 邕管經略使董昌齡誣殺參軍衡方厚，貶漵州司戶，俄徙峽州刺史。

translations.literal: The Yongguan Circuit military commissioner Dong Changling falsely accused and killed adjutant Heng Fanghou, who was demoted to Registrar of Xun Prefecture and soon transferred to Prefect of Xia Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Changling, military commissioner of Yongguan Circuit, had adjutant Heng Fanghou killed on false charges; Fanghou was demoted to registrar of Xun Prefecture, then soon made prefect of Xia.

sentences.zh: 謨諫曰：「王者赦有罪，唯故無赦。

translations.literal: Mo remonstrated: 'A ruler pardons the guilty, but never pardons repeat offenders.
translations.idiomatic: Mo remonstrated, 'A sovereign may pardon guilt, but never pardon those who offend again.

sentences.zh: 比昌齡專殺不辜，事蹟暴章，家人銜冤，萬里投訴，獄窮罪得，特被矜貸，中外以為屈法。

translations.literal: Recently Changling executed the innocent on his own authority; the facts were openly exposed, the family bore bitter wrong, and they traveled ten thousand li to plead; when the case was exhausted his guilt was proved, yet he was specially granted mercy—inside and outside the court deemed it a bending of the law.
translations.idiomatic: Changling has just murdered innocents at will—the facts are plain, the family pursued justice from afar, and though guilt was proved he was spared; court and country alike call it a miscarriage of law.

sentences.zh: 今又授刺史，復使治人，紊憲章，乖至治，不見其可。

translations.literal: Now appointing him again as prefect and again letting him govern men disorder the statutes, depart from supreme governance—I do not see how it can be allowed.
translations.idiomatic: To appoint him prefect again and set him over the people is to tangle the code and betray good government—I see no warrant for it.

sentences.zh: 」有詔改洪州別駕。

translations.literal: ' An edict changed him to Assistant Prefect of Hong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: ' An edict reassigned Changling to Assistant Prefect of Hong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞李孝本，宗室子，坐李訓事誅死，其二女沒入宮。

translations.literal: Vice Censor-in-Chief Li Xiaoben, a member of the imperial clan, was executed for involvement in Li Xun's affair; his two daughters were taken into the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiaoben of the imperial clan, Vice Censor-in-Chief, was executed in the Li Xun affair; his two daughters were seized for the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 謨上言：「陛下即位，不悅聲色，於今十年，未始采擇。

translations.literal: Mo submitted: 'Since Your Majesty took the throne you have not delighted in music and beauty; for ten years now you have not taken selections.
translations.idiomatic: Mo memorialized, 'Since Your Majesty's accession you have shunned music and courtesans; for ten years you have taken no new consorts.

sentences.zh: 數月以來，稍意聲伎，教坊閱選，百十未已，莊宅收市，沄沄有聞。

translations.literal: Over the past several months you have slightly turned your mind to music and performers; the Music Bureau has been reviewing candidates, a hundred or more without end, and purchases of estates and houses have been heard of in endless stream.
translations.idiomatic: These past months you have begun to favor music and entertainers—the Music Bureau keeps reviewing candidates by the hundred, and rumors of estate purchases run without cease.

sentences.zh: 今又取孝本女內之後宮，宗姓不育，寵倖為累，傷治道之本，速塵穢之嫌。

translations.literal: Now again taking Xiaoben's daughters into the rear palace—imperial kin not nurtured, favor and intimacy becoming a burden—this wounds the root of good governance and quickly gathers the stain of scandal.
translations.idiomatic: Now you take Xiaoben's daughters into the harem—imperial blood left unprotected, pleasure heaped upon favor—striking at the root of rule and inviting scandal.

sentences.zh: 諺曰：『止寒莫若重裘，止謗莫若自修。

translations.literal: A proverb says: 'To stop cold nothing beats a heavy fur; to stop slander nothing beats self-reform.
translations.idiomatic: The proverb runs, 'To end cold, wrap yourself in furs; to end slander, mend yourself.

sentences.zh: 』惟陛下崇千載之盛德，去一旦之玩好。

translations.literal: ' I pray Your Majesty honor the grand virtue of a thousand years and cast off a moment's diversions.
translations.idiomatic: ' I beg Your Majesty to uphold virtue that will shine for ages and put aside passing amusements.

sentences.zh: 」帝即出孝本女，詔曰：「乃祖在貞觀時，指事直言，無所避，每覽國史，朕與嘉之。

translations.literal: ' The Emperor immediately released Xiaoben's daughters; an edict said: 'Your ancestor in the Zhenguan era pointed to affairs and spoke straight without avoidance; whenever I read the national history I join in praising this.
translations.idiomatic: ' The Emperor at once released Xiaoben's daughters and proclaimed, 'Your forebear in the Zhenguan years spoke blunt truth on every matter; whenever I read the annals I admire him for it.

sentences.zh: 謨為拾遺，屢有獻納。

translations.literal: Mo as Reminder repeatedly offered submissions.
translations.idiomatic: Mo, as Reminder, offered counsel again and again.

sentences.zh: 夫備灑埽於內，非曰聲妓，恤宗女之幼，不為漁取，然疑似之間，不可戶曉，謨辭深切，其惜我之失，不亦至乎？

translations.literal: To prepare sweeping within is not called music and courtesans; to pity a clan daughter's youth is not called seizing by force—yet in what seems ambiguous one cannot make every household understand; Mo's words were deeply cutting—is not his cherishing of my faults utmost?
translations.idiomatic: Keeping the inner quarters in order is not the same as stocking courtesans; sheltering a clan girl is not the same as seizing women—yet appearances confuse, and not every household can see the difference. Mo's words cut deep; could his care for my failings be greater?

sentences.zh: 謨雖居位日淺，朕何愛一官，增直臣之氣，其以謨為右補闕。

translations.literal: Though Mo has held office but a short time, why should I begrudge one post? To increase the spirit of a straight minister—let Mo be made Right Supplementation Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Mo has served only briefly, yet why should I spare a single title? To strengthen the voice of an honest minister—appoint Mo Right Supplementation Censor.

sentences.zh: 先是，帝謂宰相曰：「太宗得徵，參裨闕失，朕今得謨，又能極諫，朕不敢仰希貞觀，庶幾處無過之地。

translations.literal: Earlier the Emperor told the chancellors: 'Taizong gained Wei Zheng to assist and repair omissions and faults; I now have Mo, who can also remonstrate to the utmost—I dare not look up hoping for Zhenguan, but perhaps I may dwell where there are no faults.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Emperor told his chancellors, 'Taizong had Wei Zheng to shore up his flaws; I now have Mo, who remonstrates just as fiercely. I dare not claim the Zhenguan age, yet perhaps I may live without grave error.

sentences.zh: 」教坊有工善為新聲者，詔授揚州司馬，議者頗言司馬品高，郎官、刺史迭處，不可以授賤工，帝意右之。

translations.literal: ' In the Music Bureau there was a craftsman skilled at new tunes; an edict appointed him Yangzhou Assistant Military Commissioner; commentators widely said the Assistant Military Commissioner rank was high—court gentlemen and prefects alternated in holding it—and it could not be given to a base craftsman; the Emperor's intent favored him.
translations.idiomatic: ' A Music Bureau artisan who excelled at new songs was made Assistant Military Commissioner of Yangzhou; critics protested that the post was too lofty for a common craftsman—the Emperor sided with the appointment.

sentences.zh: 宰相諭諫官勿復言，謨獨固諫不可，工降潤州司馬。

translations.literal: The chancellor instructed remonstrance officials not to speak again; Mo alone firmly remonstrated that it could not be, and the craftsman was demoted to Assistant Military Commissioner of Run Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor told the remonstrance officers to hold their tongues; Mo alone insisted it could not stand, and the artisan was demoted to Runzhou.

sentences.zh: 荊南監軍呂令琛縱傔卒辱江陵令，觀察使韋長避不發，移內樞密使言狀。

translations.literal: The Jingnan army supervisor Lü Lingchen let his attendants insult the Jiangling magistrate; the observation commissioner Wei Chang avoided reporting and instead sent word privately to the inner palace eunuch stating the facts.
translations.idiomatic: Army supervisor Lü Lingchen of Jingnan let his runners humiliate the magistrate of Jiangling; observation commissioner Wei Chang failed to report upward and instead whispered the facts to a inner-court eunuch.

sentences.zh: 謨劾長任察廉，知監軍侵屈官司，不以上聞，私白近臣，亂法度，請明其罰。

translations.literal: Mo impeached Chang: entrusted with inspection and integrity, knowing the army supervisor oppressed and wronged official offices yet not reporting upward, privately informing close ministers—disordering law and statutes; he requested that the penalty be made clear.
translations.idiomatic: Mo impeached Chang: charged with oversight, he knew the army supervisor had abused officialdom yet said nothing to the throne, confiding instead in court favorites— a breach of law; Mo asked that punishment be fixed.

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No response.
translations.idiomatic: The court did not reply.

sentences.zh: 俄為起居舍人，帝問：「卿家書詔頗有存者乎？

translations.literal: Soon he was made Diarist; the Emperor asked: 'Does your family preserve any of the imperial edicts?
translations.idiomatic: Soon Mo became Diarist; the Emperor asked, 'Does your family still keep any of the imperial edicts?

sentences.zh: 」謨對：「惟故笏在。

translations.literal: ' Mo replied: 'Only the old ceremonial tablet remains.
translations.idiomatic: ' Mo answered, 'Only the old court tablet remains.

sentences.zh: 」詔令上送。

translations.literal: ' An edict ordered it sent up.
translations.idiomatic: ' An edict commanded that it be sent in.

sentences.zh: 鄭覃曰：「在人不在笏。

translations.literal: Zheng Tan said: 'It is the man, not the tablet.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Tan said, 'What matters is the man, not the tablet.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「覃不識朕意，此笏乃今甘棠。

translations.literal: ' The Emperor said: 'Tan does not understand my intent—this tablet is today's sweet pear.
translations.idiomatic: ' The Emperor said, 'Tan misses my meaning—this tablet is today's sweet-pear tree under which worthies rest.

sentences.zh: 」帝因敕謨曰：「事有不當，毋嫌論奏。

translations.literal: ' The Emperor then charged Mo: 'When something is not right, do not shrink from memorializing.
translations.idiomatic: ' He then instructed Mo, 'When anything is amiss, do not hesitate to speak.

sentences.zh: 」謨對：「臣頃為諫臣，故得有所陳；

translations.literal: ' Mo replied: 'Your servant was recently a remonstrance official and so could offer statements;
translations.idiomatic: ' Mo replied, 'When I was a remonstrance officer I could speak freely;

sentences.zh: 今則記言動，不敢侵官。

translations.literal: now I record words and actions and dare not overstep my office.
translations.idiomatic: now I record conduct and dare not exceed my charge.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「兩省屬皆可議朝廷事，而毋辭也！

translations.literal: ' The Emperor said: 'Attendants of both departments may all discuss court affairs—do not decline!
translations.idiomatic: ' The Emperor said, 'Officers of both secretariats may all discuss court business—do not hold back!

sentences.zh: 」帝索起居注，謨奏：「古置左、右史，書得失，以存鑒戒。

translations.literal: ' The Emperor requested the diaries of conduct; Mo memorialized: 'Antiquity established Left and Right Historiographers to write gain and loss, to preserve mirror and warning.
translations.idiomatic: ' When the Emperor asked for the court diaries, Mo wrote, 'Antiquity set Left and Right Historiographers to record right and wrong as a mirror for rulers.

sentences.zh: 陛下所為善，無畏不書；

translations.literal: What Your Majesty does that is good—fear not that it will go unwritten;
translations.idiomatic: Your good deeds need not fear going unrecorded;

sentences.zh: 不善，天下之人亦有以記之。

translations.literal: what is not good—the people under Heaven also have those who will record it.
translations.idiomatic: your missteps—the people under Heaven will record them too.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「不然。

translations.literal: ' The Emperor said: 'Not so.
translations.idiomatic: ' The Emperor said, 'Not so.

sentences.zh: 我既嘗觀之。

translations.literal: I have already once viewed them.
translations.idiomatic: I have already looked at them once.

sentences.zh: 」謨曰：「向者取觀，史氏為失職。

translations.literal: ' Mo said: 'When you took them to view, the historiographers failed their duty.
translations.idiomatic: ' Mo said, 'When Your Majesty demanded to read them, the historians failed their office.

sentences.zh: 陛下一見，則後來所書必有諱屈，善惡不實，不可以為史，且後代何信哉？

translations.literal: Once Your Majesty has seen them, what is written afterward will surely have evasion and distortion; good and evil will not be true—it cannot serve as history, and how will later ages trust it?
translations.idiomatic: Once you have seen them, later entries will bend and hide the truth—good and evil will lie—and history will mean nothing; what will later ages believe?

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: ' Then he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: ' The Emperor desisted.

sentences.zh: 中尉仇士良捕妖民賀蘭進興及黨與治軍中，反狀且，帝自臨問，詔命斬囚以徇。

translations.literal: The Army of Inspired Strategy eunuch Qiu Shiliang arrested the sorcerer Helan Jinxing and his associates and tried them in the army; the treason case was complete, and the Emperor personally interrogated; an edict ordered the prisoners beheaded to warn the masses.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuch Qiu Shiliang of the Army of Inspired Strategy arrested the sorcerer Helan Jinxing and his band, tried them within the army, and when the treason case was complete the Emperor interrogated them himself and ordered the prisoners executed as a public warning.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞高元裕建言：「獄當與眾共之。

translations.literal: Vice Censor-in-Chief Gao Yuanyu submitted: 'Trials ought to be shared with the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Censor-in-Chief Gao Yuanyu argued, 'Trials belong to the public courts.

sentences.zh: 刑部、大理，法官也，決大獄不與知，律令謂何？

translations.literal: The Ministry of Justice and the Court of Judicial Review are the judges; deciding great cases without their knowledge—what of the statutes?
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Justice and Court of Judicial Review are the judges—how can great cases be decided without them? What becomes of the code?

sentences.zh: 請歸有司。

translations.literal: I ask that they be returned to the proper offices.
translations.idiomatic: Return the case to the proper offices.

sentences.zh: 」未報。

translations.literal: No response.
translations.idiomatic: No answer came.

sentences.zh: 謨上言：「事系軍，即推軍中。

translations.literal: Mo submitted: 'If the affair concerns the army, then try it in the army.
translations.idiomatic: Mo wrote, 'If the matter is military, try it in the army.

sentences.zh: 如齊民，宜付府縣。

translations.literal: If like common people, it should be entrusted to prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: If the accused are ordinary subjects, give them to prefecture and county.

sentences.zh: 今獄不在有司，法有輕重，何從而知？

translations.literal: Now the prison is not with the proper offices; the law has light and heavy—how can one know?
translations.idiomatic: Now the prisoners are not with the civil courts—with law's gradations hidden, who can tell fair from foul?

sentences.zh: 」帝停決，詔神策軍以官兵留仗內，余付御史台。

translations.literal: ' The Emperor halted the executions; an edict ordered the Army of Inspired Strategy to retain the officers within the guard, and the rest handed to the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: ' The Emperor stayed the executions and ordered the army to keep its officers on duty while the rest went to the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 台憚士良，不敢異，卒皆誅死。

translations.literal: The Censorate feared Shiliang and dared not differ; in the end all were executed.
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate feared Shiliang and dared not dissent; in the end all were put to death.

sentences.zh: 擢諫議大夫，兼起居舍人、弘文館直學士，謨固讓不見可，乃拜。

translations.literal: Promoted to Remonstrance Grandee, concurrently Diarist and Direct Academician of the Hongwen Institute; Mo firmly declined without approval, then accepted appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Raised to Remonstrance Grandee while serving as Diarist and academician of the Hongwen Institute, Mo declined repeatedly but at last took the posts.

sentences.zh: 始謨之進，李玨、楊嗣復實推引之。

translations.literal: At the beginning when Mo advanced, Li Jue and Yang Sifu had in fact pushed and led him.
translations.idiomatic: When Mo first rose, Li Jue and Yang Sifu had been his patrons.

sentences.zh: 武宗立，謨坐二人黨，出為汾州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wuzong acceded, Mo was implicated as a member of the two men's faction and was sent out as Prefect of Fen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuzong took the throne, Mo was tied to their faction and sent out as prefect of Fen.

sentences.zh: 俄貶信州長史。

translations.literal: Soon demoted to Long Secretary of Xin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was demoted to long secretary of Xin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 宣宗嗣位，移郢、商二州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong succeeded, he was transferred to the two prefectures of Ying and Shang.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xuanzong he served as prefect of Ying and Shang in turn.

sentences.zh: 召授給事中，遷御史中丞，發駙馬都尉杜中立奸贓，權戚縮氣。

translations.literal: Summoned and appointed Gentleman for Drafting Edicts, promoted to Censor-in-Chief, exposed the embezzlement of the Chief Commandant-Consort Du Zhongli—the powerful kin drew in their breath.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as Gentleman for Drafting Edicts and then Censor-in-Chief, he exposed the embezzlement of imperial son-in-law Du Zhongli, and the great families quailed.

sentences.zh: 俄兼戶部侍郎事，謨奏：「中丞，紀綱所寄，不宜雜領錢谷，乞專治戶部。

translations.literal: Soon concurrently handling Vice Minister of Revenue affairs, Mo memorialized: 'The Censor-in-Chief is the trust of discipline—it is not fitting to mix in charge of money and grain; I beg to specialize in governing the Revenue Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: When he was also given Revenue duties, Mo wrote, 'The Censor-in-Chief holds the empire's discipline—he should not also handle coin and grain; let me govern Revenue alone.

sentences.zh: 」詔可。

translations.literal: ' The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: ' The edict agreed.

sentences.zh: 頃之，進同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Before long, advanced to Co-Equal with the Department of the Middle and the Gate and Co-Equal of the Department of the Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly he rose to Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 建言：「今天下粗治，惟東宮未立，不早以正人傅導之，非所以存副貳之重。

translations.literal: He submitted: 'The realm today is roughly well governed; only the Eastern Palace has no established heir—if one does not early assign upright men to tutor and guide, this is not the way to preserve the weight of the heir deputy.
translations.idiomatic: He urged, 'The realm is largely at peace, yet no heir sits in the Eastern Palace—unless upright tutors are appointed soon, the weight of the succession is not secured.

sentences.zh: 」且泣下，帝為感動。

translations.literal: ' And he wept; the Emperor was moved.
translations.idiomatic: ' He wept as he spoke, and the Emperor was moved.

sentences.zh: 自敬宗後，惡言儲嫡事，故公卿無敢開陳者。

translations.literal: From Emperor Jingzong onward, ill words about establishing the heir were feared, so dukes and ministers dared not open and state them.
translations.idiomatic: Since Jingzong's day talk of the heir had been perilous, and ministers dared not broach it.

sentences.zh: 時帝春秋高，嫡嗣未辨，謨輔政，白髮其端，朝議歸重。

translations.literal: At that time the Emperor's years were advanced and the legitimate succession was not yet distinguished; Mo assisted in governance and first raised the matter at its root—court discussion turned to him with weight.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was aging and the rightful heir still unsettled; Mo in office spoke first to the heart of the matter, and court opinion rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 會詹毘國獻象，謨以為非土性，不可畜，請還其獻。

translations.literal: When Zhan Piguo presented an elephant, Mo thought it was not of the nature of the soil and could not be kept; he requested that the tribute be returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhan Piguo sent an elephant, Mo held that it was alien to the realm and should not be kept, and asked that the gift be sent back.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The edict agreed.

sentences.zh: 河東節度使李業殺降虜，邊部震擾，業內恃憑藉，人無敢言者，謨奏徙滑州。

translations.literal: The Hedong military commissioner Li Ye killed surrendered captives; the frontier departments were shaken and disturbed; Ye relied on backing within the court, and no one dared speak; Mo memorialized to transfer him to Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong commissioner Li Ye slaughtered surrendered tribesmen and unsettled the borders; shielded by court patrons, he went unchallenged until Mo had him transferred to Hua.

sentences.zh: 遷中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 大理卿馬曙有犀鎧數十首，懼而瘞之。

translations.literal: Chief Justice of the Court of Judicial Review Ma Shu had several tens of rhinoceros-hide armors; fearing discovery he buried them.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Justice Ma Shu owned dozens of rhinoceros-hide armors and, in fear, buried them.

sentences.zh: 奴王慶以怨告曙藏甲有異謀，按之無它狀，投曙嶺外，慶免。

translations.literal: The slave Wang Qing, from resentment, reported that Shu hid armor with unusual designs; investigation found no other circumstances; Shu was sent beyond the Ling range, and Qing was released.
translations.idiomatic: His slave Wang Qing, nursing a grudge, accused Shu of hoarding armor for rebellion; inquiry found no plot; Shu was exiled beyond the Ling Mountains and Qing went free.

sentences.zh: 議者謂奴訴主，法不聽。

translations.literal: Commentators said when a slave accuses his master, the law does not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Critics said the law does not hear a slave's suit against his master.

sentences.zh: 謨引律固爭，卒論慶死。

translations.literal: Mo cited the statute and firmly contended; in the end Qing was sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: Mo cited statute and fought the ruling until Qing was sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 累遷門下侍郎，兼戶部尚書。

translations.literal: Repeatedly promoted to Vice Director of the Chancellery, concurrently Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Vice Director of the Chancellery and Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 大中十年，以平章事領劍南西川節度使。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Dazhong, as Grand Councillor he headed the Jiannan West Circuit military commission.
translations.idiomatic: In Dazhong 10 he served as Grand Councillor and military commissioner of Jiannan West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 上疾求代，召拜吏部尚書，因久疾，檢校尚書右僕射、太子少保。

translations.literal: Illness worsened and he sought a replacement; summoned and appointed Minister of Personnel; because of long illness, made Acting Minister of the Right and Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Falling ill, he asked to be relieved; recalled as Minister of Personnel, he was long sick and made acting Right Vice Minister of Works and Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十六，贈司徒。

translations.literal: He died, age sixty-six; posthumously made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-six and was posthumously made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 謨為宰相，議事天子前，它相或委抑規諷，惟謨讜切無所回畏。

translations.literal: When Mo was chancellor, deliberating affairs before the Son of Heaven, other chancellors might defer and hint by regulation; only Mo spoke bluntly without turning or fear.
translations.idiomatic: As chancellor, when matters were debated before the throne other councillors might hedge and hint; Mo alone spoke straight without flinching.

sentences.zh: 宣宗嘗曰：「謨名臣孫，有祖風，朕心憚之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong once said: 'Mo is the grandson of a famous minister and has his ancestor's manner—I fear him in my heart.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong once said, 'Mo is a famous minister's grandson; he has the old family's spine—I stand in awe of him.

sentences.zh: 」然卒以剛正為令狐綯所忌，讒罷之。

translations.literal: ' Yet in the end, because of upright integrity he was envied by Linghu Tao, slandered and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: ' Yet his very uprightness drew the envy of Linghu Tao, who slandered him from office.

sentences.zh: 【贊】贊曰：君臣之際，顧不難哉！

translations.literal: 【Praise】The praise says: Between ruler and minister—surely it is not easy!
translations.idiomatic: 【Appraisal】The appraisal says: The bond between ruler and minister—how hard it is!

sentences.zh: 以徵之忠，而太宗之睿，身歿未幾，猜譖遽行。

translations.literal: With Wei Zheng's loyalty and Taizong's sagacity, not long after his body perished, suspicion and slander swiftly proceeded.
translations.idiomatic: For all Wei Zheng's loyalty and Taizong's clarity, scarcely had he died when suspicion and slander rushed in.

sentences.zh: 始，徵之諫，累數十余萬言，至君子小人，未嘗不反復為帝言之，以佞邪之亂忠也。

translations.literal: From the first, Wei Zheng's remonstrances accumulated to several hundred thousand words; on noble man and petty man he never failed repeatedly to speak to the Emperor—because flattery and evil disorder loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng's remonstrances ran to tens of thousands of words; again and again he warned the Emperor of noble men and petty men, of how sycophants poison loyalty.

sentences.zh: 久猶不免。

translations.literal: Long yet still not avoided.
translations.idiomatic: Even so, he could not escape calumny in the end.

sentences.zh: 故曰：「皓皓者易汙，嶢嶢者難全」，自古所歎雲。

translations.literal: Hence it is said: 'The bright white is easily stained; the high and steep is hard to preserve'—from antiquity what men have sighed over.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the saying: 'Pure white stains easily; lofty heights are hard to keep'—a lament since antiquity.

sentences.zh: 唐柳芳稱「徵死，知不知莫不恨惜，以為三代遺直」。

translations.literal: Tang's Liu Fang praised: 'When Wei Zheng died, whether knowing or not none failed to regret and cherish—deemed the straight line preserved from the Three Dynasties.'
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fang of Tang wrote that when Wei Zheng died, all who knew him or not grieved, calling him the straight truth the Three Dynasties had left behind.

sentences.zh: 諒哉！

translations.literal: True indeed!
translations.idiomatic: So it was!

sentences.zh: 謨之論議挺挺，有祖風烈，《詩》所謂「是以似之」者歟！

translations.literal: Mo's discourse and deliberation stood upright, with his ancestor's fierce legacy—is he not what the Odes mean by 'thus he resembles him'?
translations.idiomatic: Mo's counsel stood as straight as his forebear's fame—is he not the man the Odes mean when they say, 'In this he takes after him'?
